## Bulk one-shot remote jobs on Cloudcity (e.g. archive downloads)

The "every service must have an iTerm pane" rule covers **services** — things
that run continuously and need to be observable. **One-shot bulk jobs** with
a beginning and an end (a 519-video archive download, a 50-GB rsync, a
one-time API mirror) follow a different pattern. They don't earn a permanent
pane in `Cloudcity-Boot.app`; they live in their own working directory and
expose status via a slash command.

Codified 2026-05-20 after building `~/work/loom-mirror` — bulk Loom video
download (Loom internal GraphQL → 519 MP4s → `/Volumes/CLOUDCITY4TB/loom-mirror/`).

### The pattern

1. **Working directory on Mac Mini:** `/Users/esaruoho/work/<job>/`.
   Script + cookie/secrets + `.gitignore` live there.
2. **Output on the big SSD:** `/Volumes/CLOUDCITY4TB/<job>/` — videos, logs,
   resumable manifest. The script accepts a root-override env var
   (`LOOM_MIRROR_ROOT` for `loom-mirror`) so the working dir stays small.
3. **Detached run:** `nohup /usr/bin/python3 -u <script> >> run.log 2>&1 & disown`.
   Survives SSH disconnect. No `tmux` is installed on the Mac Mini — don't
   reach for it.
4. **Resumable manifest:** JSONL, one row per item, `status: ok | url_error | …`.
   Resume by re-running; the script reads the manifest and skips `ok` rows.
5. **Status slash from the laptop:** `/<job>-status` runs a one-call shell
   script that SSHes into the Mac Mini and reports `pgrep + manifest counts +
   tail -8 run.log + disk free`. Zero LLM in the inner loop — Claude is only
   invoked when you ask for status.

Reference implementation:

- `~/work/loom-mirror/loom-mirror.py` — the job
- `~/work/apple/bin/loom-status` — the SSH-and-report script
- `~/work/apple/commands/loom-status.md` — the slash wrapper
- `/loom-status` — installed via `~/work/apple/commands/install.sh`

### SSH gotchas re-stated for bulk jobs

- **Absolute paths in every SSH command.** SSH lands in `~`. `cd /Users/esaruoho/work/<job> && …` or `python3 /Users/esaruoho/work/<job>/script.py`.
- **The harness `<status>failed</status>` notification can lie.** When the
  bash wrapper detaches a `nohup`-launched python, the wrapper exits cleanly
  with code 0 — but the harness reports `exit code 1` (the wrapper's child
  shell returns non-zero from being detached). The actual python process is
  alive. **Always verify with `pgrep -fl <name>` before assuming death.**
- **Background polling is wasteful.** When you start a long job, drop a
  status slash and walk away; don't pile up `sleep N` checks in the LLM
  context. The work runs whether you watch or not.

### Python urllib retry gap (Python 3.9 on Mac Mini)

The Mac Mini's stock python is `/usr/bin/python3` → 3.9.6. In 3.9, **`socket.timeout` and `TimeoutError` are NOT subclasses of `urllib.error.URLError`**. A retry loop that catches only `URLError` will let read timeouts (the most common transient failure on a remote API call) escape as fatal exceptions on the first occurrence.

**Required pattern for any urllib-based retry loop on Mac Mini python:**

```python
except (urllib.error.URLError, socket.timeout, TimeoutError) as e:
    if attempt < MAX_ATTEMPTS - 1:
        time.sleep(min(2 ** attempt, 30))
        continue
    raise
```

`HTTPError` is a subclass of `URLError`, so order matters: catch `HTTPError`
first for status-code-specific logic (401 → fail fast, 429/5xx → retry),
then the timeout/connection trio above as the generic retry block.

The `loom-mirror` retry that originally caught only `URLError` let a single
30-second read timeout escape on its first video, marking a salvageable job
as `url_error`. After widening the catch and bumping read timeout 30 → 60s
with 6 attempts and 2^N backoff capped at 30s, the same video succeeded on
the retry run.

### When NOT to use this pattern

- The job is **continuously running** (not a one-shot) → it's a service, gets
  a pane in `Cloudcity-Boot.app/main.scpt` per the standard rule.
- The job needs **interactive auth** at start → run it from an iTerm pane so
  the prompt is visible.
- The job emits **events you act on in real time** (e.g. a webhook handler)
  → it's a service.

## Loom — internal GraphQL + the `regenerateMP4` trick

Documented 2026-05-20. See `~/work/loom-mirror/README.md` for the full
reference; this section is the recallable summary.

**Loom has no documented public REST API for listing/downloading videos.**
The page at `dev.loom.com/docs/record-sdk/details/api` is the Record SDK
(for embedding the recorder), not a management API. The actual surface is
`https://www.loom.com/graphql` — undocumented but stable, the same endpoint
the web app uses.

### Auth

Browser `connect.sid` cookie. Get it from DevTools → Application → Cookies
on a logged-in `loom.com` session. **Lifespan ~30 days.** Header:

```
cookie: connect.sid=s%3A…
apollographql-client-name: web
x-loom-request-source: loom_web
```

### The download path (the trick)

`getVideoTranscodedUrl` returns `null` for almost every video on the first
call. **Loom does not pre-generate MP4 URLs.** The web "Download" button
silently fires a `regenerateMP4` mutation server-side and polls — that's
why it works in the UI but not in naive scripts.

Sequence:

1. Try `getVideoTranscodedUrl(videoId, forceOriginal: false)`
2. Try `getVideoTranscodedUrl(videoId, forceOriginal: true)` (sometimes works for old originals)
3. Fire mutation:
   ```graphql
   mutation RegenerateMP4($input: RegenerateMP4Input!) {
     regenerateMP4(input: $input) { ... on RegenerateMP4Payload { success } }
   }
   ```
   with `input: {videoId, regenerationType: "DOWNLOAD"}`
4. Poll `getVideoTranscodedUrl` every 8–30s with backoff until a URL appears
5. If no URL after ~5 minutes, the video is server-side stuck — mark `no_url`
   and move on. Some Loom recordings can never be re-transcoded.

### The `list_videos` filter trap

Listing your own videos: GraphQL operation `GetLoomsForLibrary`, source
`MINE`, filter `[[{"type": "CREATED_BY_ME"}]]`. **Do not** include
`[{"type": "NOT_IN_FOLDER"}]` — the karbassi/loom-mcp upstream does, and it
silently excludes every foldered video. Esa's library had 519 videos with
`CREATED_BY_ME` only vs. ~80 with `NOT_IN_FOLDER` added.

### MCP options

- **[karbassi/loom-mcp](https://github.com/karbassi/loom-mcp)** — 58 GraphQL
  tools, cookie auth, install via `uvx` from git. Requires `brew install uv`
  on a fresh Mac.
- **[m2ai-mcp-servers/loom-mcp](https://github.com/m2ai-mcp-servers/loom-mcp)**
  — 4 tools, depends on Loom OAuth (not reliably granted). Useful only for

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""fm-worker — run Apple FoundationModels prompts that arrive in the Syncthing fm-inbox.

The 6th instance of the trigger→worker chassis (Finder tag, Voice Memo, Stickies,
Mail flag, Panel, now FM). FoundationModels — the ~3B on-device LLM behind Apple
Intelligence — only exists on macOS 26 (Tahoe). On the fleet that's the Mac Mini.
A laptop (or anything) drops a job into ~/work/comms/queue/fm-inbox/<id>.json:

    {"id": "...", "prompt": "...", "system": "...optional..."}

This worker runs `bin/fm` (the self-building Swift FoundationModels CLI sitting
next to this file), times the model wall-clock, and writes the answer to
fm-outbox/<id>.json — which Syncthing carries back to the requester:

    {"id": "...", "ok": true, "out": "...", "model_ms": 842, "host": "...", "ts": ...}

Security boundary: a job carries a prompt + optional system instruction. It never
carries a shell command — the worker only ever execs `bin/fm`. Syncthing is the
sole transport; there is no network listener.

Usage:
    fm-worker            watch the inbox forever (the daemon)
    fm-worker --once     process whatever is queued right now, then exit
    fm-worker --status   show queue depth + last heartbeat, then exit

Apple-native: python3 stdlib only; the model itself is first-party, on-device,
zero-network, zero-cost.
"""

import json
import os
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
FM = HERE / "fm"
QUEUE = Path.home() / "work" / "comms" / "queue"
INBOX = QUEUE / "fm-inbox"
OUTBOX = QUEUE / "fm-outbox"
HEARTBEAT = QUEUE / "fm-worker-heartbeat.json"
POLL_SECONDS = 1.0          # snappy: chat wants sub-2s pickup
HEARTBEAT_SECONDS = 30      # but only churn the Syncthing queue folder every 30s
RUN_TIMEOUT = 180           # a long generation can take a while on a 3B model
STALE_JOB_SECONDS = 3600    # a job nobody answered in an hour is swept


def nudge(path: Path):
    """Best-effort: make Syncthing scan + announce this path now, so the
    requester pulls the result in a second or two instead of tens of seconds."""
    try:
        subprocess.run([str(HERE / "syncthing-nudge"), str(path)],
                       capture_output=True, timeout=8)
    except Exception:
        pass


def run_fm(prompt: str, system: str) -> dict:
    """Execute bin/fm. Prompt goes on stdin (no arg-length limit); system as a flag.
    Returns ok/out/err and the model wall-clock in ms."""
    cmd = [str(FM)]
    if system:
        cmd += ["--system", system]
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    try:
        p = subprocess.run(cmd, input=prompt, capture_output=True,
                           text=True, timeout=RUN_TIMEOUT)
        ms = int((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000)
        return {"ok": p.returncode == 0, "rc": p.returncode,
                "out": (p.stdout or "").rstrip("\n"), "err": p.stderr or "",
                "model_ms": ms}
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        ms = int((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000)
        return {"ok": False, "rc": None, "out": "",
                "err": f"timed out after {RUN_TIMEOUT}s", "model_ms": ms}
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        return {"ok": False, "rc": None, "out": "", "err": str(e), "model_ms": 0}


def write_result(job_id: str, payload: dict):
    OUTBOX.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tmp = OUTBOX / f".{job_id}.tmp"
    final = OUTBOX / f"{job_id}.json"
    tmp.write_text(json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False))
    tmp.replace(final)   # atomic; Syncthing ships a complete file
    nudge(final)         # propagate back to the requester immediately


def process_one(path: Path) -> bool:
    try:
        job = json.loads(path.read_text())
    except Exception:
        return False
    prompt = job.get("prompt", "")
    if not prompt:
        # malformed; sweep if stale so it doesn't pile up
        try:
            if time.time() - path.stat().st_mtime > STALE_JOB_SECONDS:
                path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        except Exception:
            pass
        return False
    job_id = job.get("id") or path.stem
    res = run_fm(prompt, job.get("system", "") or "")
    write_result(job_id, {
        "id": job_id,
        "ok": res["ok"], "rc": res["rc"],
        "out": res["out"], "err": res["err"],
        "model_ms": res["model_ms"],
        "host": socket.gethostname().split(".")[0],
        "ts": int(time.time()),
        "from": job.get("submitter_host"),
    })
    path.unlink(missing_ok=True)   # consume the job
    return True


def beat():
    try:
        HEARTBEAT.write_text(json.dumps({"ts": int(time.time()),
                                         "host": socket.gethostname().split(".")[0]}))
    except Exception:
        pass


def scan() -> int:
    if not INBOX.is_dir():
        return 0
    handled = 0
    for p in sorted(INBOX.glob("*.json")):
        if process_one(p):
            handled += 1
    return handled


def status():
    pend = len(list(INBOX.glob("*.json"))) if INBOX.is_dir() else 0
    done = len(list(OUTBOX.glob("*.json"))) if OUTBOX.is_dir() else 0
    print(f"fm-worker · host {socket.gethostname().split('.')[0]}")
    print(f"  inbox:   {INBOX}  ({pend} prompt(s) queued)")
    print(f"  outbox:  {OUTBOX}  ({done} answer(s))")
    fmframework = Path("/System/Library/Frameworks/FoundationModels.framework")
    print(f"  FoundationModels: {'present' if fmframework.is_dir() else 'ABSENT (needs macOS 26)'}")
    if HEARTBEAT.exists():
        try:
            age = time.time() - json.loads(HEARTBEAT.read_text()).get("ts", 0)
            print(f"  last heartbeat: {age:.0f}s ago")
        except Exception:
            pass
    else:
        print("  last heartbeat: never (worker not running)")


def main() -> int:
    args = set(sys.argv[1:])
    if "-h" in args or "--help" in args:
        print(__doc__)
        return 0
    if "--status" in args:
        status()
        return 0
    INBOX.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    OUTBOX.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if "--once" in args:
        n = scan()
        beat()
        print(f"processed {n} prompt(s)")
        return 0
    # daemon
    print(f"fm-worker watching {INBOX}")
    beat()
    last_beat = time.time()
    while True:
        try:
            scan()                                  # cheap local glob, every 1s
            if time.time() - last_beat >= HEARTBEAT_SECONDS:
                beat()                              # but only churn the queue every 30s
                last_beat = time.time()
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
            print(f"  loop error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        time.sleep(POLL_SECONDS)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

file.content:
When `open Cloudcity-Boot.app` is invoked **via SSH**, iTerm `activate`s but does NOT auto-restore or create a window. The script then fails on `tell current window` with error `-1728` ("Can't get current window"), no panes spawn, and `pgrep` shows zero services even though iTerm itself is running.

`main.scpt` now defensively creates a window if none exists:

```applescript
if (count of windows) is 0 then
    create window with default profile
    delay 1
end if
```

This is a no-op for normal Login Item launches (where session restore already opened a window) and the rescue path for SSH launches.

If you ever rebuild `main.scpt` from scratch, **keep that guard** — without it, remote `!pk cloudcity restart` will silently leave the box headless. Durable backup of the previous (broken-via-SSH) version is at `~/work/comms/backups/cloudcity-boot/main.scpt.pre-ssh-window-fix-*.backup`.

Yes — a few things, some already filed, one worth its own memory.

**Already captured in `wiki/concepts/on-device-ml.md` + memory:**
- **FoundationModels is genuinely fast** — ~1s model time for a sentence; the latency you *feel* is the Syncthing round-trip (4–11s), not the LLM. Run `fm-chat` on the Mini itself to drop the transport.
- **Apple's on-device guardrails are aggressive** — two refusal shapes (hard `guardrailViolation` vs. soft in-content decline), and even benign personal-info recall ("what's my name") trips them. An FM property, not a pipeline bug.
- **The Mini's apple repo diverges via its own auto-regen commits**, so `pull --ff-only` fails on deploy → `reset --hard origin/main` is the clean path (untracked WIP survives; the divergent commits are duplicate auto-regen).
- **Don't cycle Cloudcity-Boot with a Whisper job in flight** (no resume), and **kill any stray nohup worker before cycling** or the pane's worker doubles up.

**The one not yet recorded — and it cost real time twice this session:** every `git push` to apple races the auto-regen bot, so pushes get rejected almost every time, and the rebase conflicts *only* in generated index files. Let me save the recipe so I stop relearning it:

name: feedback-apple-push-races-autoregen-bot
description: Every push to apple main races the auto-regen bot; conflicts are only in generated indexes
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Almost every `git push origin main` in the apple repo is rejected on the first try:
the auto-regen bot commits regenerated indexes (`wiki/INDEX.md`, `bin/INDEX.md`,
`scripts/workflows/INDEX.md`, `dictionaries/INDEX.md`) after each push, so origin has
moved by the time you push. The conflicts are **always and only in those generated
index files** — never in your real source.

**Why:** the pre-commit hook regenerates indexes locally AND the bot regenerates them on
origin → both sides touch the same generated files → guaranteed conflict on rebase.

**How to apply — two recipes, in order of preference:**

1. **Recommit fresh on origin/main (bulletproof, no conflict possible).** When the push is
   rejected and your commit is small, this never wedges:
   ```
   git reset --mixed HEAD~1        # uncommit; your changes go back to working tree
   git fetch origin && git reset --hard origin/main   # tracked files match remote; untracked preserved
   git add <your explicit paths>   # NEVER git add -A (hard ban — sweeps WIP)
   git commit … && git push        # fresh on top of origin → clean
   ```
   (If your files were previously untracked, reset --mixed makes them untracked again and
   reset --hard leaves them alone — re-add and commit.)

2. **Rebase + regenerate (fine when it doesn't wedge).** `git fetch && git -c rebase.autoStash=true rebase origin/main`.
   On the index conflict: regenerate (`python3 bin/wiki-index.py` / `bin/gen-skill-indexes.py`)
   rather than hand-merging, then **`git add` EVERY file** from `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U`
   (loop over all of them — resolving only one leaves others unmerged), then
   `GIT_EDITOR=true git rebase --continue`.

**The wedge trap (cost time twice):** `git rebase --continue` can keep insisting "You must
edit all merge conflicts" even when `git status` says "all conflicts fixed" and `git ls-files -u`
is empty. Don't fight it — abort and use recipe 1 (recommit fresh). See [[feedback_never_git_add_all_in_apple_repo]].

content.text:
Two answers — the quick one first, then the real one.

## Whisper resume — short version: not natively, and not worth a rebuild

The `whisper` CLI processes audio sequentially and only writes output (`.txt`/`.srt`/`.json`) **after the whole file finishes** — there's no checkpoint to resume from, by design. The only way to make a Whisper *job* resumable is to **pre-chunk the audio** (e.g. ffmpeg into 5-min pieces), transcribe each independently with a manifest, and skip completed chunks on restart. That works, but it's a real project and it costs accuracy (Whisper uses in-file context across the 30s windows; chunk edges lose that).

Given your "don't waste time on it" — **don't.** The actual problem we hit wasn't Whisper, it was *me cycling Cloudcity-Boot while a transcription might be running.* The cheap fix is what I already did tonight: **check `pgrep whisper` before any forced cycle** (repo-puller already defers for it; only a manual full cycle ignores that). So the mitigation is "gate the cycle," not "rebuild Whisper." Verdict: leave Whisper alone.

## FM chat tools — this is the good part

Let me save the design before I dump it on you (and so it survives), then walk you through it.

input.content:
# FM tools — giving the on-device LLM hands (FoundationModels tool-calling)

`bin/fm` / `fm-chat` today is a closed-book chatbot: it answers from the ~3B model's own
weights, nothing else. FoundationModels ships a **`Tool` protocol** — the model can call
Swift functions mid-generation and fold the results back into its answer. That turns the
chat from "what the model remembers" into "what the model can *go find out*" — grounded,
current, and specific to this fleet.

## How it fits our architecture (the elegant part)

Tools register on the `LanguageModelSession` **on the Mini, in-process**. So when the laptop
sends one prompt over Syncthing, the Mini's FM session can call local tools (read a file,
run an embedding search, read the climate JSON) *during that single generation* and return
the finished, grounded answer. **Tool calls do not bounce back to the laptop** — it's still
one Syncthing round-trip, no matter how many tools fire. The transport cost we measured
(~4–11s) doesn't multiply.

Implementation: extend `bin/fm.swift` to register a set of `Tool` conformers and pass them
to `LanguageModelSession(tools:instructions:)`. `fm-worker` stays unchanged (or gains a
`--tools` flag). Each tool's `call()` is a tiny Swift wrapper that either reads a file or
shells out to one of the `apple-*` CLIs already in `bin/`. Exact API surface gets verified at
build time on the Mini (FM is macOS-26-only; can't compile-test on the laptop).

## The security boundary (unchanged)

The worker's existing rule holds: **a job never carries a shell command, and FM never gets
an arbitrary-shell tool.** Tools are an *allowlist* of named, fixed-purpose Swift functions —
exactly like `panel-worker`'s registered-action allowlist. "Search this folder" is a tool;
"run this bash" is never a tool. Read-only tools first; any write/side-effect tool (send mail,
create reminder) gets added deliberately, one at a time.

## The catalog — grouped by what they reach

### A. On-device ML (already built as CLIs — these become tools almost for free)
| Tool | Wraps | "Chat can now…" |
|---|---|---|
| `semantic_search(query, folder)` | `apple-semantic-match` / `vault-grep` (NLEmbedding) | **RAG** — "find my notes about X" → grounds the answer in real files |
| `ocr(file)` | `vision-ocr` (Vision `VNRecognizeText`) | "what does this PDF/screenshot say?" |
| `image_similar(image, folder)` | `apple-image-similar` (Vision FeaturePrint) | "find the screenshot like this one / dupes" |
| `entities(text)` / `keywords(text)` | `apple-ner` / `apple-keywords` (NLTagger) | "who/what is named in this?" |
| `translate(text, lang)` | `apple-translate` (Translation framework) | "say that in Finnish" |
| `sentiment(text)` | `apple-sentiment` | tone/triage scoring |

All of these are on-device, no network, no cost — the same pedigree as FM itself.

### B. Fleet + system state (read a file or run a tiny query)
| Tool | Source | "Chat can now…" |
|---|---|---|
| `now()` | system clock | the model doesn't know the date/time — this fixes it (cheapest, highest-value first tool) |
| `home_climate()` | `~/work/comms/queue/homepod-climate/` JSON | "what's the temperature at home?" |
| `fleet_status()` | the `*-heartbeat.json` files | "is the Mini busy? is OCR running?" |
| `whisp_search(query)` | the whisp-transcripts corpus | "find where I talked about X on YouTube" |
| `mail_search(query)` | Mail SQLite (mail-flag pipeline infra) | "find emails from X" (read-only) |

### C. Apple system frameworks (Apple-native, read-only to start)
| Tool | Framework | "Chat can now…" |
|---|---|---|
| `calendar(range)` | EventKit | "what's on my calendar this week?" |
| `reminders()` | EventKit | "what's due?" |
| `contacts(name)` | Contacts | look up a person |

(These need TCC grants on the Mini; EventKit/Contacts prompts once, like the topbar grants.)

### Complement: structured output (`@Generable`)
Not a "tool" but the other half — annotate a Swift struct with `@Generable`/`@Guide` and FM
returns a **validated typed value** (constrained decoding, not parse-and-pray). This is what
makes FM a reliable *extractor* for the trigger→worker chassis: "pull the action items / the
invoice fields / the routing decision" → a struct, every time. Pairs naturally with tools
(a tool fetches text, structured output shapes the result).

## Recommended first batch (proves the three tool shapes)
1. **`now()`** — pure-compute tool, trivial, immediately useful (fixes "what day is it").
2. **`home_climate()`** — file-read tool against existing fleet data.
3. **`semantic_search(query, folder)`** — the flagship: on-device RAG via NLEmbedding, the
   one that makes the chat genuinely more than its weights.

If those three round-trip cleanly, the rest of the catalog is the same pattern repeated.

## See also
- [on-device-ml.md](on-device-ml.md) — the framework family + the fm-worker fleet plumbing
- [machine-card-protocol.md](machine-card-protocol.md) — where `fleet_status()` reads from

skill's own curated actions could be driven by an **on-device, Apple-native, zero-cost,
zero-network** model instead. You chat in plain language; FM picks the action and fills the
arguments; the action runs. That's the Automator brain, on-device. Three honest boundaries:

**1. Which tools — not all `bin/` scripts are equal.**
- ✅ **Read-only / compute / headless-batch** (OCR a folder, embed+search a vault, NER,
  translate, image-dedup, transcribe, mirror, summarize, classify) — perfect fit. These are
  what the apple skill calls "the LLM-driven Automator: any folder-batch transform." FM
  routes them beautifully.
- ⚠️ **Side-effecting UI automation** (Finder moves, app activation, window tiling, System
  Events keystrokes, sending Mail) — gated, one at a time, read-only-first. And the hard ban
  stands: **never give an LLM a System-Events-keystroke tool that fires on the machine
  someone is actively using** (see `feedback_never_ui_hijack_active_session`). Side effects go
  through side-channel pipelines (inbox files, the panel allowlist), not simulated keystrokes.

**2. Where it runs — FM is on the Mini, so it drives the *server-side* fleet.**
FM tools execute on the Mini, in-process. So FM-as-Automator-brain naturally drives the
**headless fleet** (OCR/embeddings/transcribe/mirror/translate) — not "activate an app on
the laptop I'm typing on," because that has to happen where the user is. The laptop can't
host its own FM node yet (macOS 15.6.1; FM needs 26). When the laptop is on 26, a local
fm-worker makes the same brain drive *local* actions too.

**3. It's an allowlist, not "run any script."**
FM never gets a "exec any bin/ tool" tool — that reintroduces the arbitrary-shell hole and
the UI-hijack risk. It gets a **curated set of named actions**, each a Swift `Tool` wrapper.
This is the *same allowlist* the **Apple Panel** (`apple-panel`) and **panel-worker** already
expose as cards-with-Run-buttons. So the clean unification is:

> **FM tool-calling = the natural-language front door to the Apple Panel action registry.**
> The Panel gives each capability a card + a Run button; FM lets you say it in words, picks
> the card, and fills the arg. Same curated, safe action set — two front doors.

**The capability ceiling (be honest):** a 3B model is a good *router over a defined action
set* and a good *summarize/classify/extract* engine — not a heavy multi-step reasoner. So the
realistic design is **tiered**: FM handles the fast/free/private/on-device common cases ("OCR
these, translate that, search my vault, which card fits this request"); Claude/cloud stays the
heavy reasoner for novel multi-step orchestration. FM doesn't replace Claude here — it makes
the *frequent, well-defined* automations free and local.

# FM tools — giving the on-device LLM hands (FoundationModels tool-calling)

`bin/fm` / `fm-chat` today is a closed-book chatbot: it answers from the ~3B model's own
weights, nothing else. FoundationModels ships a **`Tool` protocol** — the model can call
Swift functions mid-generation and fold the results back into its answer. That turns the
chat from "what the model remembers" into "what the model can *go find out*" — grounded,
current, and specific to this fleet.

## How it fits our architecture (the elegant part)

Tools register on the `LanguageModelSession` **on the Mini, in-process**. So when the laptop
sends one prompt over Syncthing, the Mini's FM session can call local tools (read a file,
run an embedding search, read the climate JSON) *during that single generation* and return
the finished, grounded answer. **Tool calls do not bounce back to the laptop** — it's still
one Syncthing round-trip, no matter how many tools fire. The transport cost we measured
(~4–11s) doesn't multiply.

Implementation: extend `bin/fm.swift` to register a set of `Tool` conformers and pass them
to `LanguageModelSession(tools:instructions:)`. `fm-worker` stays unchanged (or gains a
`--tools` flag). Each tool's `call()` is a tiny Swift wrapper that either reads a file or
shells out to one of the `apple-*` CLIs already in `bin/`. Exact API surface gets verified at
build time on the Mini (FM is macOS-26-only; can't compile-test on the laptop).

## The security boundary (unchanged)

The worker's existing rule holds: **a job never carries a shell command, and FM never gets
an arbitrary-shell tool.** Tools are an *allowlist* of named, fixed-purpose Swift functions —
exactly like `panel-worker`'s registered-action allowlist. "Search this folder" is a tool;
"run this bash" is never a tool. Read-only tools first; any write/side-effect tool (send mail,
create reminder) gets added deliberately, one at a time.

## The catalog — grouped by what they reach

### A. On-device ML (already built as CLIs — these become tools almost for free)
| Tool | Wraps | "Chat can now…" |
|---|---|---|
| `semantic_search(query, folder)` | `apple-semantic-match` / `vault-grep` (NLEmbedding) | **RAG** — "find my notes about X" → grounds the answer in real files |
| `ocr(file)` | `vision-ocr` (Vision `VNRecognizeText`) | "what does this PDF/screenshot say?" |
| `image_similar(image, folder)` | `apple-image-similar` (Vision FeaturePrint) | "find the screenshot like this one / dupes" |
| `entities(text)` / `keywords(text)` | `apple-ner` / `apple-keywords` (NLTagger) | "who/what is named in this?" |
| `translate(text, lang)` | `apple-translate` (Translation framework) | "say that in Finnish" |
| `sentiment(text)` | `apple-sentiment` | tone/triage scoring |

All of these are on-device, no network, no cost — the same pedigree as FM itself.

### B. Fleet + system state (read a file or run a tiny query)
| Tool | Source | "Chat can now…" |
|---|---|---|
| `now()` | system clock | the model doesn't know the date/time — this fixes it (cheapest, highest-value first tool) |
| `home_climate()` | `~/work/comms/queue/homepod-climate/` JSON | "what's the temperature at home?" |
| `fleet_status()` | the `*-heartbeat.json` files | "is the Mini busy? is OCR running?" |
| `whisp_search(query)` | the whisp-transcripts corpus | "find where I talked about X on YouTube" |
| `mail_search(query)` | Mail SQLite (mail-flag pipeline infra) | "find emails from X" (read-only) |

### C. Apple system frameworks (Apple-native, read-only to start)
| Tool | Framework | "Chat can now…" |
|---|---|---|
| `calendar(range)` | EventKit | "what's on my calendar this week?" |
| `reminders()` | EventKit | "what's due?" |
| `contacts(name)` | Contacts | look up a person |

(These need TCC grants on the Mini; EventKit/Contacts prompts once, like the topbar grants.)

### Complement: structured output (`@Generable`)
Not a "tool" but the other half — annotate a Swift struct with `@Generable`/`@Guide` and FM
returns a **validated typed value** (constrained decoding, not parse-and-pray). This is what
makes FM a reliable *extractor* for the trigger→worker chassis: "pull the action items / the
invoice fields / the routing decision" → a struct, every time. Pairs naturally with tools
(a tool fetches text, structured output shapes the result).

## Recommended first batch (proves the three tool shapes)
1. **`now()`** — pure-compute tool, trivial, immediately useful (fixes "what day is it").
2. **`home_climate()`** — file-read tool against existing fleet data.
3. **`semantic_search(query, folder)`** — the flagship: on-device RAG via NLEmbedding, the
   one that makes the chat genuinely more than its weights.

If those three round-trip cleanly, the rest of the catalog is the same pattern repeated.

## See also
- [on-device-ml.md](on-device-ml.md) — the framework family + the fm-worker fleet plumbing
- [machine-card-protocol.md](machine-card-protocol.md) — where `fleet_status()` reads from

Here's the straight picture.

## ✅ semantic_search is built — ⛔ but the Mini can't compile *any* of the tools yet

**Your `semantic_search` is done and correct** — integrated as the 6th tool alongside your `currentDateTime`/`calculator`/`unitConvert`/`systemState`/`webReader`, committed as `d2e87c0`. It uses the identical `@Generable`/`ToolOutput` pattern as your tools, so it's not the problem.

**The blocker is shared and it's an Xcode one, not a code one:**

```
xcode-select → /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools   (NOT full Xcode)
FoundationModelsMacros plugin → not present anywhere
```

`@Generable` / `@Guide` are **Swift macros**. Their compiler plugin (`FoundationModelsMacros`) ships **only with full Xcode** — CommandLineTools has no plugins at all. So `xcrun swiftc` can't expand `@Generable`, and **all 6 tools fail to compile** (the error starts at *your* first tool, `CurrentDateTimeTool`, line 58 — not mine). `-sdk` can't fix this; a plugin isn't an SDK. This is the same wall your `831d39b "-sdk"` commit was swinging at.

**The fix is one thing:** install **full Xcode 26** on the Mini, then `sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode.app`. After that, `@Generable` resolves and all six tools (semantic_search included) compile. It needs your hands — App Store / developer download, ~15 GB, and sudo. Not something I should kick off unilaterally on your always-on server.

**One thing to flag honestly:** during diagnosis I deleted the cached `fm` binary (`rm ~/.cache/apple/fm`) to force a clean rebuild. Combined with the tools version being deployed, the FM Worker's `fm` now fails to compile on every job — so **the plain chat that worked earlier tonight is down too**, until either Xcode lands or we temporarily revert `fm.swift` to the no-tools version.

channel can pass), then ONE interactive sudo round: `sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode.app

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Convert sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 to a CoreML .mlpackage.

BUILD-TIME ONLY — needs torch + transformers + coremltools in a venv (see
bin/build-minilm.sh). The runtime is pure CoreML + a hand-rolled WordPiece
tokenizer in Swift (bin/minilm-embed), zero pip deps, runs on the Neural Engine.

The exported model takes int input_ids + attention_mask (fixed length SEQ) and
returns token_embeddings [1, SEQ, 384] (the last hidden state). Sentence
embedding = attention-mask mean-pool over the tokens, done Swift-side, then L2
normalize — the standard sentence-transformers pooling.

Outputs MiniLM.mlpackage + vocab.txt to argv[1] (default ./).
"""
import os
import sys

import torch
import coremltools as ct
from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer

OUT = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "."
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
NAME = "sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2"
SEQ = 256   # all-MiniLM-L6-v2's max_seq_length; covers a paragraph chunk

print(f"[convert] loading {NAME} …", flush=True)
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(NAME)
mdl = AutoModel.from_pretrained(NAME).eval()


class Wrap(torch.nn.Module):
    """Return just last_hidden_state so the traced graph has a tensor output."""
    def __init__(self, m):
        super().__init__()
        self.m = m

    def forward(self, input_ids, attention_mask):
        return self.m(input_ids=input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask).last_hidden_state


w = Wrap(mdl).eval()
ex = tok("hello world", return_tensors="pt", padding="max_length", max_length=SEQ, truncation=True)
print("[convert] tracing …", flush=True)
with torch.no_grad():
    traced = torch.jit.trace(w, (ex["input_ids"], ex["attention_mask"]))

print("[convert] converting to CoreML …", flush=True)
mlmodel = ct.convert(
    traced,
    inputs=[
        ct.TensorType(name="input_ids", shape=ex["input_ids"].shape, dtype=int),
        ct.TensorType(name="attention_mask", shape=ex["attention_mask"].shape, dtype=int),
    ],
    compute_units=ct.ComputeUnit.ALL,
    minimum_deployment_target=ct.target.macOS14,
)
pkg = os.path.join(OUT, "MiniLM.mlpackage")
mlmodel.save(pkg)
tok.save_vocabulary(OUT)   # writes vocab.txt
# record the output feature name(s) so the Swift side knows what to read
spec = mlmodel.get_spec()
out_names = [o.name for o in spec.description.output]
print(f"[convert] SAVED {pkg}")
print(f"[convert] VOCAB {os.path.join(OUT, 'vocab.txt')}")
print(f"[convert] SEQ={SEQ} DIM=384 OUTPUTS={out_names}")

# Heavy (multi-hundred-MB download); run it nohup'd and tail the log.

VENV="$APPLE/.minilm-venv"
OUT="$APPLE/models/minilm"

content.text:
All four phases done. Here's the close-out.

## ✅ CoreML MiniLM RAG upgrade — shipped and verified

**What's now in place** (committed `c985f62`, model built on the Mini):
- `bin/build-minilm.sh` — reproducible one-time build: python3.12 venv, **pinned `transformers==4.44.2` / `torch==2.5.1` / `numpy<2`** (the numpy pin was the unlock — numpy 2 broke coremltools' int-cast).
- `bin/minilm-convert.py` — traces `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` → `models/minilm/MiniLM.mlpackage` + `vocab.txt` (gitignored).
- `bin/vault-rag` — rewritten to embed via the **CoreML MiniLM model on the Neural Engine**: hand-rolled WordPiece tokenizer → `hidden_states [1,256,384]` → mean-pool + L2-normalize. Compiled `.mlmodelc` cached; per-file vector cache v3.
- `semantic_search` (in `fm`) calls it — so `fm-chat`/`fm-submit` now get MiniLM-grounded answers.

**Proof it actually fixed the problem:**

| | NLEmbedding (before) | CoreML MiniLM (now) |
|---|---|---|
| "AppleScriptObjC ASObjC" → `asobjc.md` | not in top **30** | **#2** |
| `fm semantic_search` answer | "couldn't extract a quote" | correct, grounded summary quoting `asobjc.md` |

**Speed:** warm query ~1.2s; cold embed of the wiki ~64s, one-time on the server.

**The path was a real yak-shave** (you watched it): Xcode missing → CommandLineTools has no macro plugin → then the conversion fought transformers 5.x, torch 2.12, coremltools 9, and finally **numpy 2** was the actual culprit. All pinned now so it's reproducible.

**One known wart** (recorded, not urgent): `git reset --hard` — the deploy step — bumps file mtimes, which busts vault-rag's mtime-keyed cache, so the *next* query after each deploy pays the ~64s cold re-embed once. The clean fix is keying the cache on content hash instead of mtime — a small follow-up whenever you want it.

The retrieval is genuinely good now. That was the thing standing between `semantic_search` being a toy and being useful — and it's done.

message.content: what was the benefit of CoreML MiniLM RAG update? did this result in better situations? what is a MiniLM?

content.text:
Good questions — let me explain plainly.

## What is a MiniLM?

**MiniLM is a small AI model whose only job is to turn text into a list of numbers that captures its *meaning*.** That list (384 numbers, called an "embedding") is like a set of coordinates: two pieces of text that *mean* similar things land near each other, even if they use totally different words.

- The full name is `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`. "Mini-LM" = a shrunk-down language model (distilled from the bigger BERT family); "L6" = only 6 layers, so it's tiny (~90 MB) and fast.
- It's *fine-tuned specifically* for "similar meaning → similar numbers." That's the whole point of it. It's the standard, boring, reliable workhorse the whole industry uses for semantic search.

The thing it replaced — Apple's built-in **NLEmbedding** — does the same job, but it's an older, cruder model. Good enough to roughly sort things; not good enough to reliably know that "AppleScriptObjC" relates to your `asobjc.md` notes.

## Why the RAG needs it

The on-device chat model (the 3-billion FoundationModels one) **doesn't know what's in your notes.** RAG ("retrieval-augmented generation") fixes that: *before* the model answers, you go fetch the relevant passages from your notes and hand them over, so it answers from your actual files instead of guessing.

To "fetch the relevant passages," you have to measure meaning-similarity between the question and every passage — and that's exactly what the MiniLM embeddings are for. **Better embeddings = it finds the right passage. Worse embeddings = it finds junk.**

## Did it result in a better situation? Yes — measurably

Same question, same notes, just a better embedding model:

| Ask "what is ASObjC?" | Before (NLEmbedding) | After (MiniLM) |
|---|---|---|
| Did it find `asobjc.md`? | **Not even in the top 30** | **Ranked #2** |
| What the chat answered | "I couldn't extract a quote, just found a file path" | A correct, grounded summary quoting the file (NSFileManager, NSURL, shipped in 10.6, "most powerful tier"…) |

So `semantic_search` went from **basically useless/misleading → actually useful.** That's the benefit: it's the difference between a toy and a tool you'd trust to answer "what do my notes say about X."

**The bigger win:** this makes "chat with my own notes, on-device, private, free, no cloud" genuinely work. And it's reusable — point `vault-rag` at *any* folder (your wiki, the cc vault, the free-energy archive) and you can semantically search it.

## Keeping it honest

- It's still a *small* setup — MiniLM (retrieval) + the 3B model (answering). Great for focused lookups; not a deep reasoner.
- First search of a folder costs ~64s to embed it once (then it's cached, ~1s).
- It's a general-English model, so very obscure jargon can still be imperfect — but it's *dramatically* better than what we had.

In one line: **MiniLM is the part that lets the chat find the right page in your notes — and swapping it in is what turned semantic search from "misses the obvious" into "nails it."**

Proof's in — three different queries, old vs new, not cherry-picked:

## The proof (same notes, same queries)

**"what is ASObjC and why it matters"**
- 🔴 OLD: `how-it-was-built.md`, `automator-vs-shortcuts.md`, `wwsd-decision-tree.md` — **`asobjc.md` nowhere in sight**
- 🟢 NEW: **`asobjc.md` #1**, `log.md`, `asobjc.md` #3 — nails the actual file

**"put rich text on the macOS clipboard"**
- 🔴 OLD: #1 was `imessage-from-terminal.md` — *wrong topic*; the right file only #2
- 🟢 NEW: `clipboard-rich-text.md` in **all three** top slots — the correct doc dominates

**"read HomePod temperature and humidity"**
- 🔴 OLD: `devices/HomePod.md`, `entities/homepod.md`, `apple-panel.md`
- 🟢 NEW: **`entities/homepod.md` #1** (the actual climate-sensor doc), then a weak #2 (`data-type-chaining` — one miss), homepod again #3

So: on ASObjC the old one *completely missed*, new nails it #1. On clipboard the old one put the *wrong file* first, new is all-correct. On HomePod both are okay, new ranks the right doc first. Consistent, real improvement — not a fluke. (Side note: don't read the absolute scores as "confidence" — what matters is *which file* ranks top, and MiniLM puts the right one there.)

## The 2 shells

There are two shells in play, one per machine — and the split bit us this session:

| | Shell | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| **This laptop** | **bash 3.2.57** (`/bin/bash`) — Apple's ancient system bash | Why bash assoc-arrays/modern features are off-limits here (it's a 2007-era bash) |
| **The Mini** | **zsh** (`/bin/zsh`) — the interactive login shell | Why `timeout` failed earlier — zsh + macOS don't ship GNU `timeout` |

And a wrinkle worth knowing: on the Mini, *interactive* commands run under **zsh**, but its **service scripts deliberately use Homebrew bash 5.3.9** (`#!/usr/bin/env bash` → `/opt/homebrew/bin/bash`) — a modern bash — because the old system one is too limited. So really: laptop = old bash, Mini = zsh for shells / new bash for scripts.

That zsh-on-the-Mini fact is exactly why one of my commands tripped on `timeout` mid-build — the Mini isn't bash by default like the laptop.

content.text:
Great question — that's exactly the leap tool-calling is *for*: not "the model reasons about temperature," but "the model **runs a tool that reads the real sensor data and reports it.**" Short answer: it *can*, but there's no `home_climate` tool wired in yet (you've got `currentDateTime`/`calculator`/`unitConvert`/`systemState`/`webReader` + my `semantic_search` — none read the HomePod). So right now the chat would guess or refuse.

Let me **build it and prove it.** First, find where the live HomePod data actually is and its format (it's Syncthing-mirrored to this laptop, so I can check locally):

echo "=== existing reader tool in apple bin? ==="
ls ~/work/apple/bin/ | grep -i 'homepod\|climate' 2>/dev/null || echo "(no apple bin reader)"
echo "=== peek the freshest climate file ==="
f=$(ls -t ~/work/comms/queue/homepod-climate/* 2>/dev/null | head -1); echo "file: $f"; [ -n "$f" ] && tail -3 "$f"

"""homepod-now — print the latest HomePod climate reading, processed.

=== FoundationModelsChat/README.md ===
# FoundationModelsChat

A tiny, private chat app for **Apple's on-device LLM** (FoundationModels — the
model behind Apple Intelligence). It runs the model **in-process on your own
Mac**: no network, no account, no API key, no per-token cost. Everything you
type and everything it answers is **saved continuously**. Drag in a **PDF or
text file** and it's read and sent. Math renders natively as **MathML** via
WebKit. Fully whitelabeled — nothing here names a person, host, or service.

## Requirements

- **Apple Silicon Mac** on **macOS 26 (Tahoe)** with **Apple Intelligence enabled**
  (Settings ▸ Apple Intelligence & Siri) and the on-device model downloaded.
- The app *launches* on macOS 14+, but on anything below 26 it opens and tells
  you the model isn't available — it can't chat there.

## Build

```bash
./build.sh            # build into ./build and open
./build.sh --install  # also copy to /Applications
```

Apple-native only: AppKit, WebKit, FoundationModels, PDFKit, Vision, ImageIO.
No Homebrew, no pip, no npm, no bundled JS.

## Use

- Type, press **Enter** to send (**Shift-Enter** for a newline).
- Replies **stream in live** as the model generates them (local model).
- **Drag a PDF / .txt / .md / .rtf / image** onto the window → it's extracted to
  text (PDFKit text layer, or on-device **Vision OCR** for scans/images) and sent.
- **Paste a URL** or ask what a page says → the model calls the built-in
  **WebReader** tool to fetch it (URLSession + NSAttributedString, no third-party
  HTML parser) and answers from the text.
- The conversation **remembers** (one stateful `LanguageModelSession`). When it
  fills the on-device model's small context window, the app **summarizes and
  rebuilds the session** automatically so you can keep going.
- Equations: the model is asked to emit **MathML**, which WebKit renders with the
  system math font. (A small built-in LaTeX→MathML fallback covers `$…$` too.)

The model is **prewarmed** at launch so the first reply isn't slow.

## Where your chats go

Every turn is written immediately to:

```
~/Documents/FoundationModelsChat/<timestamp>/
  chat-<timestamp>.md     human-readable transcript
  events.jsonl            one JSON event per prompt/response
```

Nothing leaves your machine.

content.text:
Correct — they're two separate things that share the model and the word "chat." Here's the clean map (and I confirmed a key difference: the GUI runs the model *in-process* and currently has **only one tool**, WebReader; the 16 tools live in the CLI).

## Two families

**Family 1 — the CLI + Syncthing bridge** (this is where all tonight's tool demos happened):

| Piece | What it is | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| `fm` (`bin/fm` + `fm.swift`) | The engine — self-building Swift, runs FoundationModels **+ all 16 tools** in-process | **On the Mini** (macOS 26) |
| `fm-worker` | Daemon that watches `fm-inbox/`, runs `fm`, writes `fm-outbox/` (a Cloudcity-Boot pane) | On the Mini |
| `fm-submit` / `fm-chat` | Thin clients — they **don't run the model**; they post your prompt over Syncthing to the Mini's worker and print the reply. `fm-submit` = one-shot, `fm-chat` = interactive REPL | **Any Mac** (your laptop) |

→ `fm-chat` is how you reach the Mini's model **from your laptop terminal**, with homeClimate / semantic_search / fleetStatus / all 16 tools.

**Family 2 — the standalone GUI app:**

| Piece | What it is | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| `FoundationModelsChat` (`.app`, 925-line `main.swift`) | A native AppKit window — runs FoundationModels **in-process** (its own `LanguageModelSession`), streaming bubbles, drag-a-PDF, MathML. Self-contained: no worker, no bridge. Currently **one tool: WebReader** | **Only on a macOS-26 Mac** (the Mini) |

→ Pretty and interactive, but Mini-only, and it doesn't have the 16 tools yet — just WebReader + plain chat.

## So, plainly

- **Same model** (FoundationModels), **same idea of tools** — but **different code, different runtime, different tool sets.**
- `fm-chat` = terminal, reaches the Mini over Syncthing, **16 tools**, works from your laptop.
- `FoundationModelsChat` = a GUI app, runs the model **locally in its own process**, **1 tool**, only where macOS 26 exists.
- The homeClimate / ASObjC demos were the **CLI** (`fm`), not the GUI.

**Honest note on the sprawl:** there are now *two parallel implementations* of "chat with FoundationModels" — and the tools you'd want in the GUI (homeClimate, semantic_search, …) currently only exist in `fm.swift`. If the GUI is the one you actually want to live in, the real consolidation is **porting those 16 tools into `FoundationModelsChat/main.swift`** (or factoring the tools into one shared Swift file both build against) so the nice window gets the same powers as the CLI.

Want me to do that consolidation — give the GUI app the full toolset — or keep the GUI lean and lean on `fm-chat` for the tool-heavy stuff?

Got it — keep **both** chat families, and separately you want a **scriptable, no-LLM "just run the capability and get the answer" front door** that you can **Tab through** to discover/cycle what's available. That's exactly the "fat tool + thin chain coexist" idea (your own Sal rule): `fm` = the LLM picks the tool; this = *you* pick it, no model, scriptable, and Tab cycles the choices.

Let me build a first cut — a registry-driven dispatcher `apple-do` + Tab-cycling completion (bash *and* zsh), keeping it bash-3.2-safe (no assoc arrays, per the burn). I'll wire the capabilities I can do correctly right now and demo the Tab-cycle, then we expand the list.

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# apple-do — the SCRIPTABLE front door to the toolbox: pick a capability yourself,
# run it directly, get the answer. No FoundationModels, no LLM in the loop — the
# deterministic twin of `fm` (where the model picks the tool). Tab-completes and
# cycles the available capabilities (see apple-do-completion.sh).
#
#   apple-do                 list what it can do (name + one-line description)
#   apple-do <capability> …  run it
#   apple-do --complete      bare capability names, one per line (for completion)
#
# bash-3.2-safe: a case dispatch + a caps() registry, NO associative arrays.
set -uo pipefail
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"

# ── registry: one line per capability  "name<TAB>description" ──
# This is the single source of truth for the list/completion. Keep names in sync
# with the case dispatch below.
caps() {
  printf '%s\n' \
"home	current temperature + humidity at home (HomePod sensor)" \
"now	current date, time, weekday, timezone" \
"fleet	live status of the Mini's workers (heartbeats)" \
"spotlight	find files by name via Spotlight — apple-do spotlight <query>" \
"search	semantic search of your notes (MiniLM, on the Mini) — apple-do search <query>" \
"ocr	extract text from a PDF/image (Vision) — apple-do ocr <file>"
}

if [ "${1:-}" = "--complete" ]; then caps | cut -f1; exit 0; fi
if [ $# -eq 0 ] || [ "${1:-}" = "-h" ] || [ "${1:-}" = "--help" ] || [ "${1:-}" = "--list" ]; then
  echo "apple-do — scriptable capabilities (no LLM). Press Tab to cycle:"
  caps | while IFS=$'\t' read -r n d; do printf '  %-11s %s\n' "$n" "$d"; done
  exit 0
fi

cap="$1"; shift
case "$cap" in
  home)   exec "$HERE/homepod-now" ;;
  now)    date "+%A, %-d %B %Y, %H:%M %Z" ;;
  fleet)
    q="$HOME/work/comms/queue"; nowS=$(date +%s)
    for hb in "$q"/*-heartbeat.json; do
      [ -f "$hb" ] || continue
      name=$(basename "$hb" -heartbeat.json)
      age=$(( nowS - $(stat -f %m "$hb" 2>/dev/null || echo "$nowS") ))
      flag="ok"; [ "$age" -gt 180 ] && flag="STALE"
      printf '  %-26s %4ds ago  %s\n' "$name" "$age" "$flag"
    done | sort ;;
  spotlight)
    [ $# -gt 0 ] || { echo "usage: apple-do spotlight <query>"; exit 2; }
    mdfind -name "$*" 2>/dev/null | head -20 ;;
  search)
    [ $# -gt 0 ] || { echo "usage: apple-do search <query>"; exit 2; }
    # vault-rag's CoreML model lives on the Mini → run it there over SSH.
    ssh -o ConnectTimeout=6 cloudcity \
      "/Users/esaruoho/work/apple/bin/vault-rag \"$*\" --root /Users/esaruoho/work/apple/wiki --top 4" 2>/dev/null \
      || echo "apple-do: couldn't reach the Mini for semantic search." ;;
  ocr)
    [ $# -gt 0 ] || { echo "usage: apple-do ocr <file>"; exit 2; }
    exec "$HERE/vision-ocr" "$@" ;;
  *)
    echo "apple-do: unknown capability '$cap'"; echo "try: $(caps | cut -f1 | paste -sd' ' -)"; exit 2 ;;
esac

Shipped (`6428000`). You now have **both front doors, both maintained**:

- **`fm` / `fm-chat`** — the LLM picks the tool from natural language.
- **`apple-do`** — *you* pick the capability, Tab-cycles the choices, runs it directly, **no model in the loop**, scriptable.

export PATH="$HOME/work/apple/bin:$PATH"                 # so `apple-do` is callable bare

export PATH="$HOME/work/apple/bin:$PATH"
source ~/work/apple/bin/apple-do-completion.sh
```

- Type `apple-do ` then press **Tab** → it cycles `home → now → fleet → spotlight → search → ocr` (Shift-Tab cycles back). Press Enter on the one you want.

=== existing tool-ideas doc ===
---
description: Tool-calling ideas for FoundationModels (FM-on-Mini / FoundationModelsChat) — what a small on-device LLM gets POWERFUL at once it can call Apple-native tools.
---

# FM tool-calling — what else we could give the model

**The premise.** FoundationModels is a ~3B on-device model. On its own it's a decent
writer with no memory of *now*, no access to *your* data, and a tiny context
window. **Tools fix all three.** A `Tool` (name + description + `@Generable`
Arguments + `call() -> ToolOutput`) lets the model reach out, get grounded facts,
and answer from them. The model stays small; the *tools* make it capable.

Two facts that shape everything:
1. **Tools run where the model runs.** For Esa that's the **Mini** (FM-on-Mini).
   So a tool can touch the Mini's disk, the merlib archive, the apple `bin/`
   toolset, and the network — none of which the laptop-side app could do.
2. **Reliability scales with simplicity.** A 3B model calls a tool well when the
   tool has a clear name, a one-line description, and 1–3 obvious args. Keep
   tools small and read-only first; add write/destructive tools only behind
   confirmation.

Existing: **WebReaderTool** (fetch a URL → text). The categories below are what
to add, roughly in order of value-to-effort.

---

## 1. Ground the model in reality (cheap, high-value, safe)

The model literally doesn't know the date or do reliable arithmetic. These are
tiny and remove its most embarrassing failures.

- **`currentDateTime`** — returns now (date, time, weekday, timezone). `Date()` +
  `DateFormatter`. The model stops guessing "today."
- **`calculator`** — evaluate an arithmetic expression. `NSExpression`. A 3B model
  fumbles multi-digit math; offload it.
- **`unitConvert`** — length/mass/temp/etc. `Measurement` + `UnitConverter`.
- **`systemState`** — battery, disk free, thermal, uptime. So "is the Mini OK?"
  gets a real answer.

## 2. The killer category — the user's OWN knowledge (local RAG)

This is the one that matters. We spent tonight building on-device semantic search
over 600k+ embedded lines of the merlib archive (the `.npy` matrix + `vault-grep`).
**Expose that as a tool and FM becomes a grounded librarian of Esa's archive** —
retrieval is zero-token and local, the LLM only reasons over the few lines pulled.
That's retrieval-augmented generation, entirely on-device, no cloud.

- **`searchArchive`** (THE one) — `vault-grep <query> --root <corpus>` → top matching
  lines + file:line. The model cites real archive passages instead of hallucinating
  Tesla/Bearden/Schauberger claims. Pair with `vault-consilience` for cross-source.
- **`readFile`** — given a path (often returned by `searchArchive`), `file-to-text`
  it (txt/pdf/rtf/image-OCR) so the model can quote the full passage.
- **`spotlight`** — `mdfind` for files by name/content/tag across the Mac. Bridges
  the model to everything Spotlight already indexes.
- **`entities`** — `apple-ner` over a file/corpus → who/where/orgs. "Who does Wootan
  correspond with about MRA?" answered from the NER graph, not from memory.
- **`keywords`** — `apple-keywords` topical fingerprint of a folder. "What's this
  directory about?" in one call.
- **`paperLookup`** — `scihub`/DOI fetch → text, so the model can summarize a paper
  by DOI.

The strategic point: **FM (reason) × on-device embeddings (retrieve) × the archive
(truth) = a private research assistant.** Tonight's matrix-cache work is the
retrieval half; tools are the wire between them.

## 3. Apple personal data (EventKit / Contacts / Notes / Music / Mail)

All first-party, all on-device. Most need a one-time TCC grant.

- **`calendar`** — read events / "am I free Thursday?" (EventKit). Add-event behind
  confirmation.
- **`reminders`** — list/create reminders (EventKit). "Remind me to ramp the flag."
- **`contacts`** — look up a person's email/phone (Contacts). Dimillian's sample
  does exactly this.
- **`notesSearch`** — query Apple Notes (we have a Notes exporter already).
- **`nowPlaying` / `playMusic`** — read or control Music.app (ScriptingBridge).
- **`mailSearch`** — query the local Mail SQLite/.emlx (we have the mail pipeline)
  — "what did Sal say about Automator?" from the actual mailbox.

## 4. The fleet & Cloudcity (Esa-specific, the most *fun*)

FM-on-Mini already lives in the fleet. Let it act on the fleet.

- **`machineStatus`** — read a peer's published machine-card (CPU/RAM/services).
  "Is the Mini hot? Is whisp backed up?"
- **`submitOCR` / `submitTranscription`** — drop a file into the Syncthing
  inbox (the existing trigger→worker chassis). "OCR this PDF" → it just happens.
- **`runShell`** — a **whitelisted** read-only command via the file-bridge
  (`!pk run --direct`). Strictly allow-listed (ls, git status, df) — never a blank
  shell. This is the dangerous one; gate hard.
- **`homepodClimate`** — read the HomePod temp/humidity (we have the watcher).
- **`notifyPhone`** — `imessage`/`notify-iphone` to banner Esa's iPhone. "Tell me
  when the build's done" → the model pings the phone.

## 5. Web & world (network — opt-in by nature of a tool)

- **`webSearch`** — a query → top results (beyond WebReader's single-URL fetch).
- **`weather`** — WeatherKit, on-device-ish. "Coat tomorrow?"
- **`maps` / `travelTime`** — MapKit ETA between two places.

## 6. Domain tools (where Esa actually works)

- **`renoise` / `paketti`** — drive Renoise via the existing **ReMCP/OSC** bridge:
  "make an 8-step bassline," "render the song." The model as a tracker assistant.
- **`corum`** — the Tesla Extra-Coil 9-step calculator (we have the skill). "What
  voltage from a 24-inch coil at 150 kHz?" → real numbers, not a guess.
- **`rbiAnalyze`** — run the Rhythmic Balanced Interchange lens over text.
- **`gumroad` / `financing`** — "how much did I make this month?" from real data.

## 7. Vision / media

- **`ocrImage`** — Vision OCR on an image path (the laptop or Mini has Vision).
- **`imageSimilar`** — `apple-image-similar` to find dupes / "the screenshot like
  this." Visual search as a tool.
- **`transcribe`** — Speech / whisp on an audio file → text the model can use.

---

## How to actually roll these out

1. **Start with the grounding four** (date, calc, units, systemState) — trivial,
   safe, instantly make the model less dumb.
2. **Then `searchArchive` + `readFile`** — the highest-value pair; turns FM into a
   librarian of the merlib archive. This is the strategic centerpiece.
3. **Personal/fleet tools** as wanted, each behind its TCC grant.
4. **Write/destructive tools** (`runShell`, add-event, submit-jobs) **only behind an
   explicit confirmation step** and a tight allow-list. A 3B model *will*
   occasionally call the wrong tool — never let "wrong" mean "destructive."

## The honest caveats

- **3B reliability**: it'll sometimes not call a tool it should, or pass odd args.
  Clear names + minimal args + good descriptions matter more than cleverness.
- **Latency over the bridge**: each tool call is model-side on the Mini; for Esa's
  bridge usage the round-trip already costs ~6s, and a tool call adds the tool's
  own time. Fine for research, not for rapid-fire chat.
- **Tools must be registered where the model runs.** Local app = register in the
  app's `LanguageModelSession(tools:)`. Over the bridge = register in the Mini's
  `fm.swift`/worker. Same tool code, two registration sites.

## See also
- [on-device-ml.md](on-device-ml.md) — the retrieval half (`vault-grep`, the matrix cache)
- [on-device-ml-archive-applications.md](on-device-ml-archive-applications.md) — the RAG-over-archive vision
- `~/work/FoundationChat/EXAMPLES/04_Tool_Calling.md` — Apple's `Tool` protocol patterns
=== tools currently IN the GUI app ===
347:struct WebReaderTool: Tool {
417:            let session = LanguageModelSession(tools: [WebReaderTool()], instructions: FM.systemInstructions)
444:            let session = LanguageModelSession(tools: [WebReaderTool()], instructions: FM.systemInstructions)
583:        let seeded = LanguageModelSession(tools: [WebReaderTool()], instructions: instr)
=== tools in the fm CLI (for the gap) ===
"currentDateTime"
"calculator"
"unitConvert"
"systemState"
"webReader"
"semantic_search"
"readFile"
"ocr"
"entities"
"keywords"
"translate"
"sentiment"
"imageSimilar"
"spotlight"
"fleetStatus"
"homeClimate"

- **`homepodClimate`** — read the HomePod temp/humidity (we have the watcher).
- **`notifyPhone`** — `imessage`/`notify-iphone` to banner Esa's iPhone. "Tell me
  when the build's done" → the model pings the phone.

## 5. Web & world (network — opt-in by nature of a tool)

- **`webSearch`** — a query → top results (beyond WebReader's single-URL fetch).
- **`weather`** — WeatherKit, on-device-ish. "Coat tomorrow?"
- **`maps` / `travelTime`** — MapKit ETA between two places.

## 6. Domain tools (where Esa actually works)

- **`renoise` / `paketti`** — drive Renoise via the existing **ReMCP/OSC** bridge:
  "make an 8-step bassline," "render the song." The model as a tracker assistant.
- **`corum`** — the Tesla Extra-Coil 9-step calculator (we have the skill). "What
  voltage from a 24-inch coil at 150 kHz?" → real numbers, not a guess.
- **`rbiAnalyze`** — run the Rhythmic Balanced Interchange lens over text.
- **`gumroad` / `financing`** — "how much did I make this month?" from real data.

## 7. Vision / media

- **`ocrImage`** — Vision OCR on an image path (the laptop or Mini has Vision).
- **`imageSimilar`** — `apple-image-similar` to find dupes / "the screenshot like
  this." Visual search as a tool.
- **`transcribe`** — Speech / whisp on an audio file → text the model can use.

---

## How to actually roll these out

1. **Start with the grounding four** (date, calc, units, systemState) — trivial,
   safe, instantly make the model less dumb.
2. **Then `searchArchive` + `readFile`** — the highest-value pair; turns FM into a
   librarian of the merlib archive. This is the strategic centerpiece.
3. **Personal/fleet tools** as wanted, each behind its TCC grant.
4. **Write/destructive tools** (`runShell`, add-event, submit-jobs) **only behind an
   explicit confirmation step** and a tight allow-list. A 3B model *will*
   occasionally call the wrong tool — never let "wrong" mean "destructive."

## The honest caveats

- **3B reliability**: it'll sometimes not call a tool it should, or pass odd args.
  Clear names + minimal args + good descriptions matter more than cleverness.
- **Latency over the bridge**: each tool call is model-side on the Mini; for Esa's
  bridge usage the round-trip already costs ~6s, and a tool call adds the tool's
  own time. Fine for research, not for rapid-fire chat.
- **Tools must be registered where the model runs.** Local app = register in the
  app's `LanguageModelSession(tools:)`. Over the bridge = register in the Mini's
  `fm.swift`/worker. Same tool code, two registration sites.

## See also
- [on-device-ml.md](on-device-ml.md) — the retrieval half (`vault-grep`, the matrix cache)
- [on-device-ml-archive-applications.md](on-device-ml-archive-applications.md) — the RAG-over-archive vision
- `~/work/FoundationChat/EXAMPLES/04_Tool_Calling.md` — Apple's `Tool` protocol patterns

You already have a thorough catalog in `wiki/concepts/fm-tool-ideas.md` — so let me give you the *sharp* version, anchored to reality: **the GUI currently has exactly 1 tool (WebReader). The `fm` CLI has 16.** So the question splits in two.

## First: the GUI is missing 15 tools you've *already built and proven*

These exist and work in `fm.swift` right now — the nice window just doesn't have them yet. Porting them into `FoundationModelsChat`'s `LanguageModelSession(tools: [...])` is the biggest immediate win, low-risk (proven code):

`currentDateTime` · `calculator` · `unitConvert` · `systemState` · `semantic_search` (now MiniLM — actually good) · `readFile` · `ocr` · `entities` · `keywords` · `translate` · `sentiment` · `imageSimilar` · `spotlight` · `fleetStatus` · `homeClimate`

Since the GUI runs **in-process on the Mini**, each can either shell to the same `apple-*`/`vault-rag`/`homepod-now` backend (fast port — copy the `Tool` structs) or be reimplemented natively in Swift. The fast path is the copy.

## Then: the frontier — tools neither has yet (from your ideas doc), highest value first

Grounded in *your* stack, not generic:

| Tool | What it does | Backed by |
|---|---|---|
| **`calendar` / `reminders`** | "Am I free Thursday?", "remind me to ramp the flag" | EventKit (one-time TCC grant) |
| **`mailSearch`** | "what did Sal say about Automator?" from the real mailbox | your Mail SQLite + .emlx pipeline |
| **`speak`** | TTS the answer out loud | `voicebox-submit` → Mini's Voicebox |
| **`submitOCR` / `submitTranscription`** | "OCR this PDF / transcribe this" → it just happens | the Syncthing trigger→worker chassis |
| **`nowPlaying` / `playMusic`** | read/control Music | ScriptingBridge |
| **`weather`** | "coat tomorrow?" (outdoor, vs homeClimate=indoor) | WeatherKit (macOS 26) |
| **`notifyPhone`** | "ping my phone when the build's done" | `imessage`/`notify-iphone` |
| **`stashSearch`** | search the 4TB CLOUDCITY archive | `!pk stash` |
| **`corum` / `rbiAnalyze`** | Tesla coil math / RBI lens — domain answers, not guesses | your skills |
| **`renoise`** | "make an 8-step bassline" | ReMCP/OSC bridge |

## The one rule that matters

**Read-only first; anything that *acts* (send mail, run a Shortcut, submit a job, `notifyPhone`, and especially any `runShell`) goes behind a confirmation + a tight allow-list.** A 3B model *will* occasionally call the wrong tool — never let "wrong" mean "destructive." Your doc says this too; it's the load-bearing… *the critical* constraint.

## My recommendation

The clear next move is **port the 15 proven tools into the GUI** — that alone makes FoundationModelsChat as capable as the CLI, with the streaming/drag-PDF/MathML window on top. The frontier tools (calendar, mailSearch, speak) are the second wave.

Want me to do the port — bring all 15 into `FoundationModelsChat/main.swift` so the GUI Tab-… er, so the GUI has the full toolset? (I'd verify each backend's interface first, and build on the Mini since that's where it runs.) Or pick a specific few from the frontier list to build first?

---
description: Tool-calling roadmap for FoundationModels — what's built, what's next, and the three surfaces (fm CLI / apple-do / FoundationModelsChat GUI) that expose the tools. A small on-device LLM gets POWERFUL once it can call Apple-native tools.
---

# FM tool-calling — what's built, and what else to give the model

**The premise.** FoundationModels is a ~3B on-device model. On its own it's a decent
writer with no memory of *now*, no access to *your* data, and a tiny context window.
**Tools fix all three.** A `Tool` (name + description + `@Generable` Arguments +
`call()` returning a `String`/`ToolOutput`) lets the model reach out, get grounded
facts, and answer from them. The model stays small; the *tools* make it capable.

Two facts that shape everything:
1. **Tools run where the model runs.** For Esa that's the **Mini** (macOS 26). A tool
   can touch the Mini's disk, the merlib archive, the apple `bin/` toolset, the fleet
   queue, and the network — none of which the laptop (macOS 15) could do, because the
   laptop can't host FoundationModels at all.
2. **Reliability scales with simplicity.** A 3B model calls a tool well when the tool
   has a clear name, a one-line description, and 1–3 obvious args. Keep tools small and
   read-only first; add write/destructive tools only behind confirmation.

---

## The three surfaces (same tools, different front doors)

| Surface | What it is | Who picks the tool | Where it runs |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`fm` / `fm-chat`** (`bin/fm.swift`) | the CLI engine + Syncthing-bridge clients | the **LLM**, from natural language | model on the Mini; reachable from any Mac |
| **`apple-do`** (`bin/apple-do`) | scriptable, **no-LLM** runner, Tab-cycles capabilities | **you** | wherever you run it (Mini-only caps route via ssh) |
| **`FoundationModelsChat`** (GUI `.app`) | native AppKit window, streaming, drag-PDF, MathML | the **LLM**, in a window | in-process, **Mini only** (macOS 26) |

A tool is registered **where the model runs**: in `fm.swift` for the bridge, and
separately in `FoundationModelsChat/main.swift` for the GUI (same Tool code, two
registration sites). `apple-do` doesn't use the model at all — it shells straight to
the backend and prints the answer.

---

## Status — what's built (2026-06-02)

**`fm` CLI: 16 tools live.** **GUI: only WebReader (needs the other 15 ported).**
**`apple-do`: 6 capabilities wired.**

| Tool | fm CLI | GUI | apple-do | Backend |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|---|
| `currentDateTime` | ✅ | ⬜ | `now` ✅ | `Date()`+`DateFormatter` (pure Swift) |
| `calculator` | ✅ | ⬜ | — | recursive-descent parser (pure Swift) |
| `unitConvert` | ✅ | ⬜ | — | `Measurement`/`Dimension` (pure Swift) |
| `systemState` | ✅ | ⬜ | — | battery/disk/thermal |
| `webReader` | ✅ | ✅ | — | `URLSession` + HTML→text |
| `semantic_search` | ✅ | ⬜ | `search` ✅ | **`vault-rag` → CoreML MiniLM (ANE)** |
| `readFile` | ✅ | ⬜ | — | file→text |
| `ocr` | ✅ | ⬜ | `ocr` ✅ | `vision-ocr` (Vision `VNRecognizeText`) |
| `entities` | ✅ | ⬜ | — | `apple-ner` (NLTagger) |
| `keywords` | ✅ | ⬜ | — | `apple-keywords` |
| `translate` | ✅ | ⬜ | — | `apple-translate` (Translation) |
| `sentiment` | ✅ | ⬜ | — | `apple-sentiment` |
| `imageSimilar` | ✅ | ⬜ | — | `apple-image-similar` (Vision FeaturePrint) |
| `spotlight` | ✅ | ⬜ | `spotlight` ✅ | `mdfind` |
| `fleetStatus` | ✅ | ⬜ | `fleet` ✅ | reads `*-heartbeat.json` |
| `homeClimate` | ✅ | ⬜ | `home` ✅ | `homepod-now` (HomePod sensor log) |

**The headline gap:** the GUI is at 1/16. Porting the proven 15 into
`FoundationModelsChat/main.swift` is the biggest single win and is low-risk (the code
already works in `fm.swift`).

---

## 1. Ground the model in reality — DONE ✅ (cheap, high-value, safe)

The model literally doesn't know the date or do reliable arithmetic. All four shipped
in the `fm` CLI; trivial to port to the GUI.

- **`currentDateTime`** ✅ — now (date/time/weekday/timezone). The model stops guessing "today."
- **`calculator`** ✅ — safe recursive-descent arithmetic (no `NSExpression`/eval; can't crash).
- **`unitConvert`** ✅ — length/mass/temp/volume/duration via `Measurement`.
- **`systemState`** ✅ — battery, disk free, thermal, uptime → "is the Mini OK?".

## 2. The killer category — the user's OWN knowledge (local RAG) — DONE + UPGRADED ✅

This is the one that matters, and it's now genuinely good.

- **`semantic_search`** ✅ — chunks notes into header-aware **sections**, embeds each via
  **`all-MiniLM-L6-v2` as a CoreML model on the Neural Engine** (`bin/vault-rag`), ranks
  chunks, returns quotable passages. **The upgrade was decisive:** with the old
  `NLEmbedding`, "AppleScriptObjC" couldn't surface `asobjc.md` even in the top 30; with
  MiniLM it's **#2**, and the chat gives a correct grounded answer. Retrieval is local +
  zero-token; the LLM only reasons over the few passages pulled. RAG, entirely on-device.
- **`readFile`** ✅ — given a path, file→text (txt/pdf/rtf/image-OCR) so the model can quote
  the full passage.
- **`spotlight`** ✅ — `mdfind` for files by name/content/tag across the Mac.
- **`entities`** ✅ / **`keywords`** ✅ — `apple-ner` / `apple-keywords` over a file/folder.
- **Still ideas:** **`searchArchive`** over the full 600k-line merlib corpus (point
  `vault-rag --root` at the archive, warm its cache once); **`paperLookup`** (DOI →
  `scihub` → text → summarize); **`consilience`** (`vault-consilience` cross-source).

The strategic point: **FM (reason) × MiniLM embeddings (retrieve) × the archive (truth)
= a private research assistant.** The MiniLM swap was the retrieval half finally working.

## 3. Apple personal data (EventKit / Contacts / Notes / Music / Mail) — IDEAS ⬜

All first-party, all on-device. Most need a one-time TCC grant (prompt once, like the
AppleToolbox grants).

- **`calendar`** — read events / "am I free Thursday?" (EventKit). Add-event behind confirmation.
- **`reminders`** — list/create reminders (EventKit). "Remind me to ramp the flag."
- **`contacts`** — look up a person's email/phone (Contacts).
- **`notesSearch`** — query Apple Notes (the Notes exporter already exists).
- **`nowPlaying` / `playMusic`** — read or control Music.app (ScriptingBridge).
- **`mailSearch`** — query the local Mail SQLite/.emlx (the mail-flag pipeline already reads
  it) — "what did Sal say about Automator?" from the actual mailbox. Read-only; **never**
  poll Mail via osascript (see `mail-app-internal-behaviors.md`).

## 4. The fleet & Cloudcity (Esa-specific, the most *fun*) — PARTLY DONE

FM-on-Mini already lives in the fleet. Let it act on the fleet.

- **`fleetStatus`** ✅ — reads the published heartbeats. "Is whisp backed up? Is the Mini hot?"
- **`homeClimate`** ✅ — HomePod temp/humidity from the watcher log (`homepod-now`).
- **`submitOCR` / `submitTranscription`** ⬜ — drop a file into the Syncthing inbox (the
  existing trigger→worker chassis). "OCR this PDF" → it just happens.
- **`speak`** ⬜ — TTS the answer via `voicebox-submit` → the Mini's Voicebox. A GUI app you
  live in is the natural place for "read it to me."
- **`notifyPhone`** ⬜ — `imessage`/`notify-iphone` to banner the iPhone. "Tell me when the
  build's done." (write — behind confirmation.)
- **`stashSearch`** ⬜ — query the 4TB CLOUDCITY archive (`!pk stash`).
- **`runShell`** ⬜ — a **whitelisted, read-only** command via the file-bridge. Strictly
  allow-listed (`ls`, `git status`, `df`) — **never a blank shell.** The dangerous one; gate hard.

## 5. Web & world (network — opt-in by nature) — PARTLY DONE

- **`webReader`** ✅ — fetch a URL → readable text (in BOTH the CLI and the GUI already).
- **`webSearch`** ⬜ — a query → top results (beyond a single-URL fetch). No clean Apple-native
  search API; would need a provider — weigh against the no-third-party pedigree.
- **`weather`** ⬜ — WeatherKit, "coat tomorrow?" (outdoor, vs `homeClimate` = indoor).
- **`travelTime`** ⬜ — MapKit ETA between two places.

## 6. Domain tools (where Esa actually works) — IDEAS ⬜

- **`renoise` / `paketti`** — drive Renoise via the existing **ReMCP/OSC** bridge:
  "make an 8-step bassline," "render the song." The model as a tracker assistant.
- **`corum`** — the Tesla Extra-Coil 9-step calculator (the skill exists). "What voltage from
  a 24-inch coil at 150 kHz?" → real numbers, not a guess.
- **`rbiAnalyze`** — run the Rhythmic Balanced Interchange lens over text.
- **`gumroad` / `financing`** — "how much did I make this month?" from real data (the `gumroad`
  CLI exists).

## 7. Vision / media — PARTLY DONE

- **`ocr`** ✅ — Vision OCR on a file/image (`vision-ocr`). Also covered by the GUI's drag-drop.
- **`imageSimilar`** ✅ — `apple-image-similar` → find dupes / "the screenshot like this one."
- **`transcribe`** ⬜ — Speech / whisp on an audio file → text the model can use.

---

## Build infrastructure & gotchas (learned the hard way, 2026-06-02)

- **`@Generable` needs FULL XCODE on the build machine.** The macro plugin
  (`FoundationModelsMacros`) ships only with Xcode, NOT CommandLineTools — without it
  `swiftc` fails with *"external macro implementation type … could not be found."* `-sdk`
  doesn't help (a plugin isn't an SDK). Install Xcode 26, then once: `sudo xcode-select -s
  /Applications/Xcode.app && sudo xcodebuild -license accept && sudo xcodebuild -runFirstLaunch`.
- **The MiniLM CoreML model** is built by `bin/build-minilm.sh` → `bin/minilm-convert.py`
  (python3.12 venv). **Pin `transformers==4.44.2` `torch==2.5.1` `numpy<2`** — numpy 2 breaks
  coremltools' int-cast (*"only 0-dimensional arrays can be converted to Python scalars"*),
  and coremltools dropped ONNX input, so `torch.jit.trace` + numpy<2 is the path. The
  `.mlpackage`+`vocab.txt` live in `models/minilm/` (gitignored); the compiled `.mlmodelc` is
  cached at `~/.cache/apple/`.
- **Two registration sites.** A tool exists for the model only where it's registered: the
  Mini's `fm.swift` `groundingTools` array (bridge/CLI) AND the GUI's
