---
description: Tool-calling roadmap for FoundationModels — what's built, what's next, and the three surfaces (fm CLI / apple-do / FoundationModelsChat GUI) that expose the tools. A small on-device LLM gets POWERFUL once it can call Apple-native tools.
---

# FM tool-calling — what's built, and what else to give the model

**The premise.** FoundationModels is a ~3B on-device model. On its own it's a decent
writer with no memory of *now*, no access to *your* data, and a tiny context window.
**Tools fix all three.** A `Tool` (name + description + `@Generable` Arguments +
`call()` returning a `String`/`ToolOutput`) lets the model reach out, get grounded
facts, and answer from them. The model stays small; the *tools* make it capable.

Two facts that shape everything:
1. **Tools run where the model runs.** For Esa that's the **Mini** (macOS 26). A tool
   can touch the Mini's disk, the merlib archive, the apple `bin/` toolset, the fleet
   queue, and the network — none of which the laptop (macOS 15) could do, because the
   laptop can't host FoundationModels at all.
2. **Reliability scales with simplicity.** A 3B model calls a tool well when the tool
   has a clear name, a one-line description, and 1–3 obvious args. Keep tools small and
   read-only first; add write/destructive tools only behind confirmation.

---

## The three surfaces (same tools, different front doors)

| Surface | What it is | Who picks the tool | Where it runs |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`fm` / `fm-chat`** (`bin/fm.swift`) | the CLI engine + Syncthing-bridge clients | the **LLM**, from natural language | model on the Mini; reachable from any Mac |
| **`apple-do`** (`bin/apple-do`) | scriptable, **no-LLM** runner, Tab-cycles capabilities | **you** | wherever you run it (Mini-only caps route via ssh) |
| **`FoundationModelsChat`** (GUI `.app`) | native AppKit window, streaming, drag-PDF, MathML | the **LLM**, in a window | in-process, **Mini only** (macOS 26) |

A tool is registered **where the model runs**: in `fm.swift` for the bridge, and
separately in `FoundationModelsChat/main.swift` for the GUI (same Tool code, two
registration sites). `apple-do` doesn't use the model at all — it shells straight to
the backend and prints the answer.

---

## Status — what's built (2026-06-02)

**`fm` CLI: 16 tools live.** **GUI: only WebReader (needs the other 15 ported).**
**`apple-do`: 6 capabilities wired.**

| Tool | fm CLI | GUI | apple-do | Backend |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|---|
| `currentDateTime` | ✅ | ⬜ | `now` ✅ | `Date()`+`DateFormatter` (pure Swift) |
| `calculator` | ✅ | ⬜ | — | recursive-descent parser (pure Swift) |
| `unitConvert` | ✅ | ⬜ | — | `Measurement`/`Dimension` (pure Swift) |
| `systemState` | ✅ | ⬜ | — | battery/disk/thermal |
| `webReader` | ✅ | ✅ | — | `URLSession` + HTML→text |
| `semantic_search` | ✅ | ⬜ | `search` ✅ | **`vault-rag` → CoreML MiniLM (ANE)** |
| `readFile` | ✅ | ⬜ | — | file→text |
| `ocr` | ✅ | ⬜ | `ocr` ✅ | `vision-ocr` (Vision `VNRecognizeText`) |
| `entities` | ✅ | ⬜ | — | `apple-ner` (NLTagger) |
| `keywords` | ✅ | ⬜ | — | `apple-keywords` |
| `translate` | ✅ | ⬜ | — | `apple-translate` (Translation) |
| `sentiment` | ✅ | ⬜ | — | `apple-sentiment` |
| `imageSimilar` | ✅ | ⬜ | — | `apple-image-similar` (Vision FeaturePrint) |
| `spotlight` | ✅ | ⬜ | `spotlight` ✅ | `mdfind` |
| `fleetStatus` | ✅ | ⬜ | `fleet` ✅ | reads `*-heartbeat.json` |
| `homeClimate` | ✅ | ⬜ | `home` ✅ | `homepod-now` (HomePod sensor log) |

**The headline gap:** the GUI is at 1/16. Porting the proven 15 into
`FoundationModelsChat/main.swift` is the biggest single win and is low-risk (the code
already works in `fm.swift`).

---

## 1. Ground the model in reality — DONE ✅ (cheap, high-value, safe)

The model literally doesn't know the date or do reliable arithmetic. All four shipped
in the `fm` CLI; trivial to port to the GUI.

- **`currentDateTime`** ✅ — now (date/time/weekday/timezone). The model stops guessing "today."
- **`calculator`** ✅ — safe recursive-descent arithmetic (no `NSExpression`/eval; can't crash).
- **`unitConvert`** ✅ — length/mass/temp/volume/duration via `Measurement`.
- **`systemState`** ✅ — battery, disk free, thermal, uptime → "is the Mini OK?".

## 2. The killer category — the user's OWN knowledge (local RAG) — DONE + UPGRADED ✅

- **`semantic_search`** ✅ — chunks notes into header-aware **sections**, embeds each via
  **`all-MiniLM-L6-v2` as a CoreML model on the Neural Engine** (`bin/vault-rag`), ranks
  chunks, returns quotable passages. **The upgrade was decisive:** with the old
  `NLEmbedding`, "AppleScriptObjC" couldn't surface `asobjc.md` even in the top 30; with
  MiniLM it's **#2**, and the chat gives a correct grounded answer. Retrieval is local +
  zero-token; the LLM only reasons over the few passages pulled. RAG, entirely on-device.

  the full passage.
- **`spotlight`** ✅ — `mdfind` for files by name/content/tag across the Mac.
- **`entities`** ✅ / **`keywords`** ✅ — `apple-ner` / `apple-keywords` over a file/folder.

  `vault-rag --root` at the archive, warm its cache once); **`paperLookup`** (DOI →
  `scihub` → text → summarize); **`consilience`** (`vault-consilience` cross-source).

= a private research assistant.** The MiniLM swap was the retrieval half finally working.

## 3. Apple personal data (EventKit / Contacts / Notes / Music / Mail) — IDEAS ⬜

AppleToolbox grants).

- **`calendar`** — read events / "am I free Thursday?" (EventKit). Add-event behind confirmation.
- **`reminders`** — list/create reminders (EventKit). "Remind me to ramp the flag."
- **`contacts`** — look up a person's email/phone (Contacts).
- **`notesSearch`** — query Apple Notes (the Notes exporter already exists).
- **`nowPlaying` / `playMusic`** — read or control Music.app (ScriptingBridge).
- **`mailSearch`** — query the local Mail SQLite/.emlx (the mail-flag pipeline already reads
  it) — "what did Sal say about Automator?" from the actual mailbox. Read-only; **never**
  poll Mail via osascript (see `mail-app-internal-behaviors.md`).

## 4. The fleet & Cloudcity (Esa-specific, the most *fun*) — PARTLY DONE

FM-on-Mini already lives in the fleet. Let it act on the fleet.

- **`fleetStatus`** ✅ — reads the published heartbeats. "Is whisp backed up? Is the Mini hot?"
- **`homeClimate`** ✅ — HomePod temp/humidity from the watcher log (`homepod-now`).
- **`submitOCR` / `submitTranscription`** ⬜ — drop a file into the Syncthing inbox (the
  existing trigger→worker chassis). "OCR this PDF" → it just happens.
- **`speak`** ⬜ — TTS the answer via `voicebox-submit` → the Mini's Voicebox. A GUI app you
  live in is the natural place for "read it to me."
- **`notifyPhone`** ⬜ — `imessage`/`notify-iphone` to banner the iPhone. "Tell me when the
  build's done." (write — behind confirmation.)
- **`stashSearch`** ⬜ — query the 4TB CLOUDCITY archive (`!pk stash`).
- **`runShell`** ⬜ — a **whitelisted, read-only** command via the file-bridge. Strictly
  allow-listed (`ls`, `git status`, `df`) — **never a blank shell.** The dangerous one; gate hard.

## 5. Web & world (network — opt-in by nature) — PARTLY DONE

- **`webReader`** ✅ — fetch a URL → readable text (in BOTH the CLI and the GUI already).
- **`webSearch`** ⬜ — a query → top results (beyond a single-URL fetch). No clean Apple-native
  search API; would need a provider — weigh against the no-third-party pedigree.
- **`weather`** ⬜ — WeatherKit, "coat tomorrow?" (outdoor, vs `homeClimate` = indoor).
- **`travelTime`** ⬜ — MapKit ETA between two places.

## 6. Domain tools (where Esa actually works) — IDEAS ⬜

- **`renoise` / `paketti`** — drive Renoise via the existing **ReMCP/OSC** bridge:
  "make an 8-step bassline," "render the song." The model as a tracker assistant.
- **`corum`** — the Tesla Extra-Coil 9-step calculator (the skill exists). "What voltage from
  a 24-inch coil at 150 kHz?" → real numbers, not a guess.
- **`rbiAnalyze`** — run the Rhythmic Balanced Interchange lens over text.
- **`gumroad` / `financing`** — "how much did I make this month?" from real data (the `gumroad`
  CLI exists).

## 7. Vision / media — PARTLY DONE

- **`ocr`** ✅ — Vision OCR on a file/image (`vision-ocr`). Also covered by the GUI's drag-drop.
- **`imageSimilar`** ✅ — `apple-image-similar` → find dupes / "the screenshot like this one."
- **`transcribe`** ⬜ — Speech / whisp on an audio file → text the model can use.

- **`transcribe`** ⬜ — Speech / whisp on an audio file → text the model can use.

## Build infrastructure & gotchas (learned the hard way, 2026-06-02)

- **`@Generable` needs FULL XCODE on the build machine.** The macro plugin
  (`FoundationModelsMacros`) ships only with Xcode, NOT CommandLineTools — without it
  `swiftc` fails with *"external macro implementation type … could not be found."* `-sdk`
  doesn't help (a plugin isn't an SDK). Install Xcode 26, then once: `sudo xcode-select -s
  /Applications/Xcode.app && sudo xcodebuild -license accept && sudo xcodebuild -runFirstLaunch`.
- **The MiniLM CoreML model** is built by `bin/build-minilm.sh` → `bin/minilm-convert.py`
  (python3.12 venv). **Pin `transformers==4.44.2` `torch==2.5.1` `numpy<2`** — numpy 2 breaks
  coremltools' int-cast (*"only 0-dimensional arrays can be converted to Python scalars"*),
  and coremltools dropped ONNX input, so `torch.jit.trace` + numpy<2 is the path. The
  `.mlpackage`+`vocab.txt` live in `models/minilm/` (gitignored); the compiled `.mlmodelc` is
  cached at `~/.cache/apple/`.
- **Two registration sites.** A tool exists for the model only where it's registered: the
  Mini's `fm.swift` `groundingTools` array (bridge/CLI) AND the GUI's
  `LanguageModelSession(tools:)` in `FoundationModelsChat/main.swift`. Porting a tool to the
  GUI = copy its `Tool` struct into `main.swift` and add it to that array.
- **`apple-do` is the no-model twin.** Same capabilities, no FoundationModels — `bin/apple-do`
  shells straight to the backend (or routes Mini-only ones like `search` over ssh).
  `bin/apple-do-completion.sh` gives bash+zsh **Tab-cycling** of the capability names.
- **Deploy busts the RAG cache.** `git reset --hard` (the Mini deploy step) bumps file mtimes,
  so `vault-rag`'s mtime-keyed cache cold-re-embeds the corpus on the next query (~64 s,
  one-time per deploy). Fix later by keying the cache on content hash, not mtime.

## How to roll the rest out

1. **Port the 15 proven tools into the GUI** — the biggest single win; the GUI becomes as
   capable as the CLI, with streaming + drag-PDF + MathML on top.
2. **Personal/fleet second wave** — `calendar`, `mailSearch`, `speak`, `submitOCR`, `weather`.
3. **Write/destructive tools** (`runShell`, add-event, submit-jobs, `notifyPhone`) **only
   behind explicit confirmation + a tight allow-list.** A 3B model *will* occasionally call
   the wrong tool — never let "wrong" mean "destructive."

## The honest caveats

- **3B reliability**: it'll sometimes not call a tool it should, or pass odd args. Clear names
  + minimal args + good descriptions matter more than cleverness.
- **Latency over the bridge**: each tool call is model-side on the Mini; the Syncthing
  round-trip already costs ~4–11 s, and a tool call adds the tool's own time. Fine for
  research, not rapid-fire chat. (The GUI, in-process, has no bridge hop.)
- **Aggressive guardrails**: Apple's on-device safety layer refuses readily (even benign
  personal-info recall). Rephrasing usually clears it; it's an FM property, not a bug.

# FM tool-calling — what else we could give the model

**The premise.** FoundationModels is a ~3B on-device model. On its own it's a decent
writer with no memory of *now*, no access to *your* data, and a tiny context
window. **Tools fix all three.** A `Tool` (name + description + `@Generable`
Arguments + `call() -> ToolOutput`) lets the model reach out, get grounded facts,
and answer from them. The model stays small; the *tools* make it capable.

Two facts that shape everything:
1. **Tools run where the model runs.** For Esa that's the **Mini** (FM-on-Mini).
   So a tool can touch the Mini's disk, the merlib archive, the apple `bin/`
   toolset, and the network — none of which the laptop-side app could do.
2. **Reliability scales with simplicity.** A 3B model calls a tool well when the
   tool has a clear name, a one-line description, and 1–3 obvious args. Keep
   tools small and read-only first; add write/destructive tools only behind
   confirmation.

Existing: **WebReaderTool** (fetch a URL → text). The categories below are what
to add, roughly in order of value-to-effort.

---

## 1. Ground the model in reality (cheap, high-value, safe)

The model literally doesn't know the date or do reliable arithmetic. These are
tiny and remove its most embarrassing failures.

- **`currentDateTime`** — returns now (date, time, weekday, timezone). `Date()` +
  `DateFormatter`. The model stops guessing "today."
- **`calculator`** — evaluate an arithmetic expression. `NSExpression`. A 3B model
  fumbles multi-digit math; offload it.
- **`unitConvert`** — length/mass/temp/etc. `Measurement` + `UnitConverter`.
- **`systemState`** — battery, disk free, thermal, uptime. So "is the Mini OK?"
  gets a real answer.

## 2. The killer category — the user's OWN knowledge (local RAG)

This is the one that matters. We spent tonight building on-device semantic search
over 600k+ embedded lines of the merlib archive (the `.npy` matrix + `vault-grep`).
**Expose that as a tool and FM becomes a grounded librarian of Esa's archive** —
retrieval is zero-token and local, the LLM only reasons over the few lines pulled.
That's retrieval-augmented generation, entirely on-device, no cloud.

- **`searchArchive`** (THE one) — `vault-grep <query> --root <corpus>` → top matching
  lines + file:line. The model cites real archive passages instead of hallucinating
  Tesla/Bearden/Schauberger claims. Pair with `vault-consilience` for cross-source.
- **`readFile`** — given a path (often returned by `searchArchive`), `file-to-text`
  it (txt/pdf/rtf/image-OCR) so the model can quote the full passage.
- **`spotlight`** — `mdfind` for files by name/content/tag across the Mac. Bridges
  the model to everything Spotlight already indexes.
- **`entities`** — `apple-ner` over a file/corpus → who/where/orgs. "Who does Wootan
  correspond with about MRA?" answered from the NER graph, not from memory.
- **`keywords`** — `apple-keywords` topical fingerprint of a folder. "What's this
  directory about?" in one call.
- **`paperLookup`** — `scihub`/DOI fetch → text, so the model can summarize a paper
  by DOI.

The strategic point: **FM (reason) × on-device embeddings (retrieve) × the archive
(truth) = a private research assistant.** Tonight's matrix-cache work is the
retrieval half; tools are the wire between them.

## 3. Apple personal data (EventKit / Contacts / Notes / Music / Mail)

All first-party, all on-device. Most need a one-time TCC grant.

- **`calendar`** — read events / "am I free Thursday?" (EventKit). Add-event behind
  confirmation.
- **`reminders`** — list/create reminders (EventKit). "Remind me to ramp the flag."
- **`contacts`** — look up a person's email/phone (Contacts). Dimillian's sample
  does exactly this.
- **`notesSearch`** — query Apple Notes (we have a Notes exporter already).
- **`nowPlaying` / `playMusic`** — read or control Music.app (ScriptingBridge).
- **`mailSearch`** — query the local Mail SQLite/.emlx (we have the mail pipeline)
  — "what did Sal say about Automator?" from the actual mailbox.

## 4. The fleet & Cloudcity (Esa-specific, the most *fun*)

FM-on-Mini already lives in the fleet. Let it act on the fleet.

- **`machineStatus`** — read a peer's published machine-card (CPU/RAM/services).
  "Is the Mini hot? Is whisp backed up?"
- **`submitOCR` / `submitTranscription`** — drop a file into the Syncthing
  inbox (the existing trigger→worker chassis). "OCR this PDF" → it just happens.
- **`runShell`** — a **whitelisted** read-only command via the file-bridge
  (`!pk run --direct`). Strictly allow-listed (ls, git status, df) — never a blank
  shell. This is the dangerous one; gate hard.
- **`homepodClimate`** — read the HomePod temp/humidity (we have the watcher).
- **`notifyPhone`** — `imessage`/`notify-iphone` to banner Esa's iPhone. "Tell me
  when the build's done" → the model pings the phone.

## 5. Web & world (network — opt-in by nature of a tool)

- **`webSearch`** — a query → top results (beyond WebReader's single-URL fetch).
- **`weather`** — WeatherKit, on-device-ish. "Coat tomorrow?"
- **`maps` / `travelTime`** — MapKit ETA between two places.

## 6. Domain tools (where Esa actually works)

- **`renoise` / `paketti`** — drive Renoise via the existing **ReMCP/OSC** bridge:
  "make an 8-step bassline," "render the song." The model as a tracker assistant.
- **`corum`** — the Tesla Extra-Coil 9-step calculator (we have the skill). "What
  voltage from a 24-inch coil at 150 kHz?" → real numbers, not a guess.
- **`rbiAnalyze`** — run the Rhythmic Balanced Interchange lens over text.
- **`gumroad` / `financing`** — "how much did I make this month?" from real data.

## 7. Vision / media

- **`ocrImage`** — Vision OCR on an image path (the laptop or Mini has Vision).
- **`imageSimilar`** — `apple-image-similar` to find dupes / "the screenshot like
  this." Visual search as a tool.
- **`transcribe`** — Speech / whisp on an audio file → text the model can use.

---

## How to actually roll these out

1. **Start with the grounding four** (date, calc, units, systemState) — trivial,
   safe, instantly make the model less dumb.
2. **Then `searchArchive` + `readFile`** — the highest-value pair; turns FM into a
   librarian of the merlib archive. This is the strategic centerpiece.
3. **Personal/fleet tools** as wanted, each behind its TCC grant.
4. **Write/destructive tools** (`runShell`, add-event, submit-jobs) **only behind an
   explicit confirmation step** and a tight allow-list. A 3B model *will*
   occasionally call the wrong tool — never let "wrong" mean "destructive."

## The honest caveats

- **3B reliability**: it'll sometimes not call a tool it should, or pass odd args.
  Clear names + minimal args + good descriptions matter more than cleverness.
- **Latency over the bridge**: each tool call is model-side on the Mini; for Esa's
  bridge usage the round-trip already costs ~6s, and a tool call adds the tool's
  own time. Fine for research, not for rapid-fire chat.
- **Tools must be registered where the model runs.** Local app = register in the
  app's `LanguageModelSession(tools:)`. Over the bridge = register in the Mini's
  `fm.swift`/worker. Same tool code, two registration sites.

Let me write a Python script that pulls the 15 tools + `runCLI`/`Calc`/`Units` from `fm.swift` (verbatim, source of truth), `@available`-guards the structs, injects them into `main.swift` with a `ToolEnv` + `fmTools()` factory, and routes all three session sites through it:

input.command:
cd /Users/esaruoho/work/apple
python3 - <<'PYEOF'
import re, pathlib

fm = pathlib.Path("bin/fm.swift").read_text().splitlines()
main_path = pathlib.Path("FoundationModelsChat/main.swift")
main = main_path.read_text()

# names to port (exclude WebReaderTool + WebText — GUI has its own WebReader)
wanted = [
    ("CurrentDateTimeTool", True), ("Calc", False), ("CalculatorTool", True),
    ("Units", False), ("UnitConvertTool", True), ("SystemStateTool", True),
    ("SemanticSearchTool", True), ("runCLI", False), ("ReadFileTool", True),
    ("OCRTool", True), ("EntitiesTool", True), ("KeywordsTool", True),
    ("TranslateTool", True), ("SentimentTool", True), ("ImageSimilarTool", True),
    ("SpotlightTool", True), ("FleetStatusTool", True), ("HomeClimateTool", True),
]

def find_start(name):
    pats = [rf'^struct {name}: Tool ', rf'^enum {name} ', rf'^func {name}\(']
    for i, ln in enumerate(fm):
        if any(re.match(p, ln) for p in pats):
            return i
    raise SystemExit(f"NOT FOUND: {name}")

def block(start):
    # capture decl line .. first subsequent line that is exactly '}'
    for j in range(start+1, len(fm)):
        if fm[j].rstrip() == '}':
            return fm[start:j+1]
    raise SystemExit("no close for line %d" % start)

parts = []
for name, is_tool in wanted:
    b = block(find_start(name))
    text = "\n".join(b)
    if is_tool:
        text = "@available(macOS 26.0, *)\n" + text
    parts.append(text)

tool_env = '''// ── ToolEnv: where the ported tools find the apple bin/ + the RAG corpus.
// Whitelabel-safe: NSHomeDirectory() (no hardcoded username), env-overridable.
enum ToolEnv {
    static let binDir = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["FM_BIN_DIR"]
        ?? "\\(NSHomeDirectory())/work/apple/bin"
    static let searchDir = ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["FM_SEARCH_DIR"]
        ?? "\\(NSHomeDirectory())/work/apple/wiki"
}
'''

factory = '''@available(macOS 26.0, *)
func fmTools() -> [any Tool] {
    [
        WebReaderTool(),
        CurrentDateTimeTool(), CalculatorTool(), UnitConvertTool(), SystemStateTool(),
        SemanticSearchTool(searchDir: ToolEnv.searchDir, binDir: ToolEnv.binDir),
        ReadFileTool(binDir: ToolEnv.binDir), OCRTool(binDir: ToolEnv.binDir),
        EntitiesTool(binDir: ToolEnv.binDir), KeywordsTool(binDir: ToolEnv.binDir),
        TranslateTool(binDir: ToolEnv.binDir), SentimentTool(binDir: ToolEnv.binDir),
        ImageSimilarTool(binDir: ToolEnv.binDir), SpotlightTool(),
        FleetStatusTool(), HomeClimateTool(),
    ]
}
'''

inject = ("\n// ───────── ported from bin/fm.swift for CLI⇄GUI parity (15 tools) ─────────\n"
          + tool_env + "\n" + "\n\n".join(parts) + "\n\n" + factory
          + "// ───────── end ported tools ─────────\n\n")

# insert right before the GUI's WebReaderTool availability line
anchor = "@available(macOS 26.0, *)\nstruct WebReaderTool: Tool {"
assert anchor in main, "WebReaderTool anchor not found"
main = main.replace(anchor, inject + anchor, 1)

# route all three session sites through fmTools()
before = main.count("LanguageModelSession(tools: [WebReaderTool()]")
main = main.replace("LanguageModelSession(tools: [WebReaderTool()]",
                    "LanguageModelSession(tools: fmTools()")
main_path.write_text(main)
print(f"ported {len(parts)} blocks; rewired {before} session site(s)")
print("structs added:", ", ".join(n for n,t in wanted if t))
PYEOF

## Why it's happening

The chat keeps **one stateful `LanguageModelSession` for the whole conversation.** A stateful session feeds the model the **entire prior conversation on every turn** — that *is* "re-reading all the conversations above." It's how chat memory works: turn 3 is answered with turns 1–2 in full context.

The instructions now explicitly tell it: **answer only the latest message, don't fold in earlier topics, only call a directly-relevant tool.** Combined with the fast-path (home/fleet/date never enter the model's context) and "New chat" (resets memory), the topic-bleed should be gone.

This is the nature of a **small (3B) model with conversation memory**: every turn it re-reads the whole chat, and it anchors on whatever the conversation has been about. Three levers manage it, strongest first:

Resonance is not an energy source
Resonance is a condition of efficient energy exchange between two storage elements — electric ↔ magnetic in an LC circuit, kinetic ↔ potential in a pendulum, the O–H stretch in a vibrating molecule. At resonance a small drive can build up a large amplitude (high node voltage, large vibrational displacement) because the loss per cycle is small. But that amplitude was paid for by the drive. Resonance stores and concentrates energy; it does not create it. "Resonance alone," with no energy input, splits no water. This is simply conservation of energy.
Splitting water has a fixed thermodynamic price
Decomposing liquid water into H₂ and O₂ costs a minimum amount of energy that no technique — DC, AC, pulsed, microwave, plasma, or "resonant" — can undercut:
Reversible (Gibbs) minimum: ΔG° = +237 kJ per mole of H₂, equivalent to a cell potential of 1.23 V at 25 °C, 1 atm.
Thermoneutral (enthalpy) value: ΔH° = +286 kJ/mol, equivalent to 1.48 V — the point at which the cell neither heats nor cools itself.
Below 1.23 V electrolysis cannot proceed at all; between 1.23 and 1.48 V it runs only by absorbing heat from its surroundings. These floors come from the state functions of water itself, not from the apparatus — so changing the waveform of the input cannot move them.
What resonance can legitimately do
Real, peer-reviewed work shows resonant and pulsed excitation can push a real cell closer to the thermodynamic floor by trimming loss mechanisms — never past it:
Pulsed / PWM electrolysis lets the diffusion layer relax between pulses, cutting concentration overpotential and recovering a few percent.
Series electrical resonance lets a supply deliver high instantaneous voltage at the cell with low source current, improving coupling.
Microwave-, RF-, and plasma-assisted (contact-glow-discharge) electrolysis are genuine and studied — but each consumes more net energy, not less; they buy reaction rate or selectivity with extra input.
Every one of these is "resonance-assisted electrolysis." None is "hydrogen from resonance alone," and none beats 1.23 V.
The molecular-resonance idea, specifically
The seductive picture: water's O–H bond has natural vibrational frequencies (the stretching modes sit near 3650–3760 cm⁻¹, about 110–113 THz), so if you "resonate" the bond it should snap. Two facts kill this as a free route:
The first O–H bond dissociation energy is ~498 kJ/mol. To break it you must deposit at least that much energy into the bond by some path. Resonance changes the coupling efficiency, never the amount required.
Liquid water is strongly hydrogen-bonded. Its vibrational modes are hugely broadened and de-phase in well under a picosecond. Energy pumped into one mode thermalizes into heat almost immediately, so you cannot accumulate it in a single bond to "ring it apart." This is why bond-selective laser dissociation works only for isolated gas-phase molecules, at large energy cost — not in bulk liquid water.
The historical claims
Devices claiming net hydrogen from "water resonance" — most famously Stanley Meyer's Water Fuel Cell — have not survived independent measurement. Meyer's was ruled "gross and egregious fraud" by an Ohio court in 1996, after the demonstrated gas output proved consistent with ordinary electrolysis powered by the input current. The recurring measurement errors are well documented: mistaking reactive volt-amperes for real watts, mis-integrating spiky pulse waveforms, and ignoring energy already stored in the system.
Bottom line
The original sentence is right, and the reason is sharper than "it doesn't work": resonance is a coupling phenomenon, not an energy source, and water-splitting has a thermodynamic floor — 1.23 V, or 237 kJ per mole of H₂ — set by water's own state functions. Resonant and pulsed techniques are real and can nudge a cell toward that floor, but nothing, resonant or otherwise, produces hydrogen from water without paying at least that price in energy.

Rebuilt clean and relaunched (PID 49756) — new build is in your screen-share.

## What actually happened (from the transcript)

You **pasted a long essay** and the model — instead of discussing it — **invented "web pages to fetch" and called `WebReader`**, which failed → *"unable to fetch the specified web pages."* There was no URL anywhere in your message. The tool's own description said *"call whenever the user asks what a web page says,"* and a 3B model reads "mentions sources" as "go fetch pages." The `null` you saw earlier is the same family — a tool firing when it shouldn't and returning nothing.

## The fix (just shipped)

- **`WebReader` now fires only on an explicit `http(s)://` URL** in your message — never to "find sources" or "verify."
- **System instructions now say:** when you paste text and ask it to discuss/continue, just do that — don't fetch anything, and never claim it tried to fetch a page.

## To verify

Hit **⌘N (New Chat)** first — the current session is *primed* on the failed WebReader attempt, so it'll keep wanting to fetch. Fresh chat clears that. Then paste your essay again and ask it to continue/critique — it should engage with the text directly now.

## The honest meta-point

This is the recurring theme: **a 3B model + 16 tools misfires** — it grabs the wrong tool (WebReader here, homeClimate earlier). The strongest lever is **tool descriptions** (tightened WebReader), then **New chat** to clear primed context, then the fast-path (known intents skip the model entirely). It won't be perfectly reliable — that's the model size, not the wiring. If a specific prompt still produces `null` or a wrong tool after a fresh chat, screenshot that exact prompt and I'll tighten the offending tool the same way.

Yes — `null` means it broke (the model produced an empty/garbage generation). And now I can name the **root cause of all three symptoms** (null, instant "context full" → compact → crash, and echoing instead of discussing):

**The 16 tools are overflowing the model's tiny context window.** FoundationModels has a ~4096-token window. Every turn, *all 16 tool schemas* (each tool's name + description + argument schema) get injected into that window — that's a big chunk gone before you type anything. Add a long pasted essay and it's instantly full → the model can't reason (so it echoes or returns `null`), and "continue in new convo" re-sends the same giant essay into another 16-tool session → overflow again → the compaction path crashes.

So the **parity you asked for (16 model tools) is literally what's breaking the GUI.** A 3B/4096 model can't hold that many tools *and* a real conversation. This is a genuine trade-off and it's your call how to resolve it:

content.text:
Built clean, launched (PID 10306) — the new **lean chat** is in your screen-share.

## Straight answers

**"Are tools actually fucking up the chat?"** — **Yes, definitively.** That was the whole problem. The 16 tool schemas were injected into the ~4,096-token window *every turn*, eating ~1,500–2,500 tokens before your text. Your essay then overflowed → "context exhausted" → compaction → still overflowed → **`null`** (the model had no room to generate) and crashes. `null` = it broke, every time, for exactly that reason.

**Your essay's size:** ~**3,900 characters ≈ ~1,000 tokens.** On its own that fits fine in 4,096. It was *only* a problem stacked on top of the 16 tool schemas. **With tools gone, your ~1,000-token essay leaves ~3,000 tokens for the reply — plenty.** You wouldn't approach the wall until roughly **~10,000+ characters** of input.

## What I built (your design)

- **The model now arms ZERO tools** → full context window → reliable, discusses pasted text instead of echoing/null-ing.
- **Tools run in a harness *before* the model** (`directAnswer`): "home temperature", "fleet", "what time" → run the script, return instantly, never touch the model. Exactly the "process tools before sending to FoundationModels" you asked for.
- Instructions now tell it to **engage pasted text in its own words, don't repeat it.**

## Test it

**⌘N (New Chat)** first — the current session is poisoned by the crash. Then paste your resonance essay and ask *"critique this"* or *"continue this"* → it should discuss it, no `null`, no crash, no echo.

Two optional add-ons, your call:
- **Input guard** — warn/trim if you paste >~10k chars (so you never hit the wall by surprise).
- **Expand the harness** — add "search my notes about X" / URL-fetch as pre-model intents, so the lean chat keeps those capabilities without arming the model.

Built clean, launched (PID 31197).

## Why it said "oh, internet"

It's a **small-model reflex**, not a search question and not your wiring. Instruction-tuned 3B models, when hit with a factual/technical (and especially *fringe*, like free-energy) topic, reflexively hedge with *"I can't access external resources / search the web"* — even though they **know the topic and don't need the web at all** (it gave you a great electrolysis answer earlier). There are no tools in the lean chat now, so nothing was actually trying to search — the model just *said* that as a deflection.

## What I just fixed

1. **Instructions now forbid that deflection** and affirm it: *"You have broad built-in knowledge — ANSWER FROM IT. You do not have, and do not need, the internet. NEVER say you can't access external resources or search the web — just discuss the topic."*
2. **`null`/empty replies now map to a real message** ("⚠️ The model returned an empty reply — ⌘N for a fresh chat or shorten the message") instead of a bare `null`.

## Test

**⌘N first** — your current session is primed on both the deflection and the earlier crash, so it'll keep misbehaving. In a fresh chat, *"i want to talk about resonance based electrolysis of water into hydrogen"* should make it engage from its own knowledge.

## Honest caveat + the robust next step

The instruction *reduces* the deflection but a 3B model won't obey 100%. If it still deflects, the bulletproof fix is a **programmatic auto-retry**: detect the deflection phrase in the reply ("don't have access", "can't search the web") and automatically re-ask once with a "answer from your own knowledge" nudge — so you never see the deflection even when the model reflexes. Want me to add that? It's the reliable cure for the reflex; the instruction change is the cheap first attempt.

## Yes — the prompt is now exposed and editable, live

**Prompt ▸ Edit System Prompt…** (or **⇧⌘P**) opens a panel showing the exact text that colors every reply — the same instructions we've been editing in code, now editable *in the app*:

- Edit it → **Save** → it applies immediately and starts a fresh chat, so you watch how the new prompt changes the model's behavior turn-by-turn.
- **Reset to Default** restores the built-in seed.
- It **persists** (UserDefaults) across relaunches, so your custom prompt sticks.

This is exactly your idea: the system prompt is the dial that colors responses, and now you can turn it yourself and see the effect — no rebuild, no code.

## Things to try in it

- Persona: *"You are a terse Renoise tracker expert. Answer in ≤3 sentences."* → watch replies get short + domain-flavored.
- Style: *"Always answer as a skeptical physicist who demands sources."*
- The anti-deflection line is in there now (*"never say you can't access the web"*) — you can see/tune that directly, which is the lever for the "oh internet" reflex.

Because the chat is lean (no tools fighting for the window), the prompt is now the **main** control over behavior — so this editor is the right place to shape it. Experiment freely; if a prompt makes it misbehave, ⇧⌘P → Reset to Default.

One thing to keep in mind: the prompt counts against the ~4,096-token window too, so a *huge* prompt eats room your conversation needs — keep it punchy. If you land on a prompt you love, tell me and I'll make it the new default in code so every fresh install gets it.

Made fleet-usable 2026-06-01 as the 6th instance of the trigger→worker chassis:

  while-true wrapper, survives reboots; stateless so a boot cycle mid-job is harmless.
- `bin/fm-submit "prompt"` — one-shot from any Mac (`--wait`/`--system`/`--status`).
- `bin/fm-chat` — live REPL, conversation memory replayed client-side.

**FM tool-calling needs FULL XCODE on the build machine (RESOLVED 2026-06-02).** `@Generable`/
`@Guide` (the macros every FoundationModels `Tool` argument struct uses) require the
`FoundationModelsMacros` compiler plugin, which ships ONLY with full Xcode — NOT with
CommandLineTools. The Mini had only CommandLineTools → `xcrun swiftc` failed with "external
macro implementation type 'FoundationModelsMacros.GenerableMacro' could not be found; plugin
for module 'FoundationModelsMacros' not found" (and `-sdk` does NOT fix it — a plugin is not an
SDK). **Fix that worked:** install Xcode (`xcodes install --latest` → Xcode 26.5; needs Esa's
Apple ID + 2FA + sudo — `mas`/`xcodes`/`sudo` all hit interactive-auth walls no automated
channel can pass), then ONE interactive sudo round: `sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode.app
&& sudo xcodebuild -license accept && sudo xcodebuild -runFirstLaunch`. After that `fm --check`
→ available and all 6 tools compile. (No-sudo alternative for the build step alone:
`DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer`.) **semantic_search verified live**:
"global keyboard shortcuts" → correctly surfaced `lessons/global-hotkeys-and-snapengine.md`.
See [[zero_roundtrip_pattern]].

**semantic_search RAG: CoreML MiniLM SHIPPED and works (2026-06-02).** `bin/vault-rag` chunks
notes into header-aware sections and embeds via **all-MiniLM-L6-v2 as a CoreML model on the
Neural Engine** (hand-rolled WordPiece tokenizer, input_ids+attention_mask [1,256] → hidden_states
[1,256,384], mean-pool + L2-normalize, cosine=dot). Verified: "AppleScriptObjC ASObjC" surfaces
`concepts/asobjc.md` at **#2** (was NOT in the top 30 with NLEmbedding), and `fm semantic_search`

func applicationDidFinishLaunching(_ note: Notification) {
        let frame = NSRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: 820, height: 720)
        window = NSWindow(contentRect: frame,
                          styleMask: [.titled, .closable, .miniaturizable, .resizable],
                          backing: .buffered, defer: false)
        window.title = "FoundationModels Chat"
        window.center()
        window.setFrameAutosaveName("FMChatWindow")

        let root = DropView(frame: frame)
        root.autoresizingMask = [.width, .height]
        root.registerForDraggedTypes([.fileURL])
        root.onDrop = { [weak self] urls in self?.ingest(urls) }
        window.contentView = root

        // transcript
        let webConf = WKWebViewConfiguration()
        let ucc = WKUserContentController()
        ucc.add(self, name: "fmchat")   // HTML buttons post back here
        webConf.userContentController = ucc
        webView = WKWebView(frame: NSRect(x: 0, y: 110, width: 820, height: 610), configuration: webConf)
        webView.autoresizingMask = [.width, .height]
        webView.setValue(false, forKey: "drawsBackground")
        root.addSubview(webView)

        // input
        let inputScroll = NSScrollView(frame: NSRect(x: 12, y: 12, width: 690, height: 88))
        inputScroll.autoresizingMask = [.width]
        inputScroll.hasVerticalScroller = true
        inputScroll.borderType = .lineBorder
        inputView = NSTextView(frame: inputScroll.bounds)
        inputView.autoresizingMask = [.width]
        inputView.font = NSFont.systemFont(ofSize: 14)
        inputView.isRichText = false
        inputView.delegate = self
        inputView.textContainerInset = NSSize(width: 6, height: 6)
        inputScroll.documentView = inputView
        root.addSubview(inputScroll)

        sendButton = NSButton(frame: NSRect(x: 712, y: 12, width: 96, height: 88))
        sendButton.autoresizingMask = [.minXMargin]
        sendButton.title = "Send"
        sendButton.bezelStyle = .rounded
        sendButton.keyEquivalent = "\r"
        sendButton.target = self
        sendButton.action = #selector(sendTapped)
        root.addSubview(sendButton)

# Apple Translation — supported languages (Finnish is NOT supported)

**Verified 2026-06-02 on CloudcityMacMini (macOS 26.3)** by querying the Translation
framework directly:

```swift
import Translation
let langs = await LanguageAvailability().supportedLanguages   // [Locale.Language]
```

## The supported set — 19 languages

```
ar  de  en  es  fr  hi  id  it  ja  ko  nl  pl  pt  ru  th  tr  uk  vi  zh
```

Arabic, German, English, Spanish, French, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese,
Korean, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Thai, Turkish, Ukrainian, Vietnamese,
Chinese. (The raw list returns `en` and `zh` twice for regional variants → 21 entries,
19 distinct languages.)

## Finnish is NOT supported — and neither is any Nordic/Baltic language

`supportedLanguages.contains("fi")` → **NO.** Also absent: Swedish (sv), Norwegian (no),
Danish (da), Estonian, Latvian, Lithuanian, etc. So **you cannot install a Finnish⇄English
translation pack — there is no such pack.** The Translate.app / "Translation Languages"
settings list simply does not offer Finnish.

## The bigger consequence: no on-device Finnish at all on this stack

Two separate Apple on-device systems both refuse Finnish:

1. **Translation framework** — Finnish not in `supportedLanguages` (above).
2. **FoundationModels** (the on-device LLM) — a Finnish prompt throws
   `LanguageModelSession.GenerationError.unsupportedLanguageOrLocale` ("Unsupported
   language"). See [on-device-ml.md](on-device-ml.md).

So the FoundationModelsChat translation harness (detect non-English → translate to English
→ model → translate back) **works for the 18 non-English supported languages, but NOT for
Finnish.** A Finnish bedtime story for Tomas needs a *cloud* translator/model (or a
third-party on-device model with Finnish), not Apple's on-device stack.

**Practical rule for the harness:** if the detected language isn't in the 19-language set,
say plainly "Apple Translation doesn't support that language — write in English"; do NOT
tell the user to install a pack that doesn't exist (the 2026-06-02 bug Esa caught).

## How to re-verify (if Apple adds languages later)

Run the probe above on the target Mac; compare `supportedLanguages` to this list. Apple
expands the set over OS releases, so Finnish may appear in a future macOS — re-check before
assuming it's still absent.

## See also
- [on-device-ml.md](on-device-ml.md) — FoundationModels + the on-device framework family
- [fm-tool-ideas.md](fm-tool-ideas.md) — the FoundationModelsChat tool/harness roadmap
- `bin/apple-translate` — the CLI the harness shells to (Translation framework via a hidden SwiftUI host)

Deployed the resize fix (PID 61530) — let me know if the chat fills the window now.

On memory — here's the **how**, and it's exactly how *my* memory works (the `~/.claude` files you've watched me use all session):

**FoundationModels can't remember on its own** — tiny ~4096-token window, and each session is wiped on New Chat. So memory has to be **external**: a `memory.md` file that gets **injected into the prompt every session** (so the model always "knows" it), and that the **chat writes to**. Three pieces:

1. **Store** — `~/Documents/FoundationModelsChat/memory.md` (durable facts about you).
2. **Inject (read)** — prepend it to the system prompt each session: *"Things you know about the user: …"*. Now every reply is colored by it.
3. **Affect (write)** — the chat updates it: a `remember: …` command appends a fact, a `⇧⌘M` editor lets you curate it, and the new memory takes effect on the next turn.

That's a memory the chat *affects* and the model *uses* — reliable and under your control. (The fancier "model auto-decides what to remember" is possible but a 3B is unreliable at it; I'd layer that on top later.)

Let me build that v1. Reading the prompt/file region to add the memory infrastructure:

content.text:
Shipped + verified (PID 77892, binary has the memory feature). You now have a memory the chat affects and the model reads:

## How to use it

- **Teach it:** type `remember: I have a 5-year-old son named Tomas` → it appends to memory and confirms *"🧠 Added to memory"* (no model call, instant). Variants work: "remember that…", "note that…".
- **It persists across chats:** the memory is **injected into every session's prompt**, so after a New Chat the model still knows it. Ask *"what's my son's name?"* in a fresh chat → it answers from memory.
- **Curate it:** **⇧⌘M** opens a Memory editor (view/edit/clear). `clear memory` in chat wipes it.
- **It's a real file:** `~/Documents/FoundationModelsChat/memory.md` — editable in any editor, backable-up, diffable.

## Architecture (the "how")

It's exactly the pattern you've watched *me* use all session: the model can't remember on its own (4k window, wiped per chat), so memory lives **outside** the model — a file that **seeds the prompt** (read) and that the **chat updates** (write). `fullInstructions = system prompt + memory`, capped at 1500 chars so it can't blow the window.

## Test it

`remember: my son is Tomas, age 5` → New Chat (⌘N) → *"what should I do this weekend with my kid?"* → it should factor in a 5-year-old named Tomas.

**Honest limits:** memory eats context tokens (keep it tight — it's capped), and a 3B model uses injected facts imperfectly (it'll reference them but not flawlessly). The reliable, user-controlled core (you decide what it remembers) is what's built. If you later want it to **auto-decide** what to remember as you talk, that's a follow-up — but it's less reliable on a 3B, so explicit `remember:` is the solid foundation.

---
description: Apple's on-device Translation framework supports only 19 languages — Finnish is NOT one of them (verified 2026-06-02). Combined with FoundationModels also rejecting Finnish, there is no on-device path to Finnish on this stack.
---

# Apple Translation — supported languages (Finnish is NOT supported)

**Verified 2026-06-02 on CloudcityMacMini (macOS 26.3)** by querying the Translation
framework directly:

```swift
import Translation
let langs = await LanguageAvailability().supportedLanguages   // [Locale.Language]
```

## The supported set — 19 languages

```
ar  de  en  es  fr  hi  id  it  ja  ko  nl  pl  pt  ru  th  tr  uk  vi  zh
```

Arabic, German, English, Spanish, French, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese,
Korean, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Thai, Turkish, Ukrainian, Vietnamese,
Chinese. (The raw list returns `en` and `zh` twice for regional variants → 21 entries,
19 distinct languages.)

## Finnish is NOT supported — and neither is any Nordic/Baltic language

`supportedLanguages.contains("fi")` → **NO.** Also absent: Swedish (sv), Norwegian (no),
Danish (da), Estonian, Latvian, Lithuanian, etc. So **you cannot install a Finnish⇄English
translation pack — there is no such pack.** The Translate.app / "Translation Languages"
settings list simply does not offer Finnish.

## The bigger consequence: no on-device Finnish at all on this stack

Two separate Apple on-device systems both refuse Finnish:

1. **Translation framework** — Finnish not in `supportedLanguages` (above).
2. **FoundationModels** (the on-device LLM) — a Finnish prompt throws
   `LanguageModelSession.GenerationError.unsupportedLanguageOrLocale` ("Unsupported
   language"). See [on-device-ml.md](on-device-ml.md).

So the FoundationModelsChat translation harness (detect non-English → translate to English
→ model → translate back) **works for the 18 non-English supported languages, but NOT for
Finnish.** A Finnish bedtime story for Tomas needs a *cloud* translator/model (or a
third-party on-device model with Finnish), not Apple's on-device stack.

**Practical rule for the harness:** if the detected language isn't in the 19-language set,
say plainly "Apple Translation doesn't support that language — write in English"; do NOT
tell the user to install a pack that doesn't exist (the 2026-06-02 bug Esa caught).

## How to re-verify (if Apple adds languages later)

Run the probe above on the target Mac; compare `supportedLanguages` to this list. Apple
expands the set over OS releases, so Finnish may appear in a future macOS — re-check before
assuming it's still absent.

## See also
- [on-device-ml.md](on-device-ml.md) — FoundationModels + the on-device framework family
- [fm-tool-ideas.md](fm-tool-ideas.md) — the FoundationModelsChat tool/harness roadmap
- `bin/apple-translate` — the CLI the harness shells to (Translation framework via a hidden SwiftUI host)

name: fm-worker-fleet-llm
description: Apple FoundationModels (on-device LLM) is usable from any Mac via the fm-worker on the Mini
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fde596bb-669f-493a-8a43-04a4e33cd964
---

FoundationModels — Apple's ~3B on-device LLM (~65k context, the model behind Apple
Intelligence) — only exists on macOS 26, so on the fleet it lives on the **Mac Mini**.
Made fleet-usable 2026-06-01 as the 6th instance of the trigger→worker chassis:

- `bin/fm-worker` (Mini): watches `~/work/comms/queue/fm-inbox/`, runs `bin/fm` (the
  self-building Swift FoundationModels CLI), writes answers to `fm-outbox/`. Runs as the
  **"FM Worker" pane in Cloudcity-Boot** (graduated from nohup 2026-06-02) — crash-only
  while-true wrapper, survives reboots; stateless so a boot cycle mid-job is harmless.
- `bin/fm-submit "prompt"` — one-shot from any Mac (`--wait`/`--system`/`--status`).
- `bin/fm-chat` — live REPL, conversation memory replayed client-side.

**FM tool-calling needs FULL XCODE on the build machine (RESOLVED 2026-06-02).** `@Generable`/
`@Guide` (the macros every FoundationModels `Tool` argument struct uses) require the
`FoundationModelsMacros` compiler plugin, which ships ONLY with full Xcode — NOT with
CommandLineTools. The Mini had only CommandLineTools → `xcrun swiftc` failed with "external
macro implementation type 'FoundationModelsMacros.GenerableMacro' could not be found; plugin
for module 'FoundationModelsMacros' not found" (and `-sdk` does NOT fix it — a plugin is not an
SDK). **Fix that worked:** install Xcode (`xcodes install --latest` → Xcode 26.5; needs Esa's
Apple ID + 2FA + sudo — `mas`/`xcodes`/`sudo` all hit interactive-auth walls no automated
channel can pass), then ONE interactive sudo round: `sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode.app
&& sudo xcodebuild -license accept && sudo xcodebuild -runFirstLaunch`. After that `fm --check`
→ available and all 6 tools compile. (No-sudo alternative for the build step alone:
`DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer`.) **semantic_search verified live**:
"global keyboard shortcuts" → correctly surfaced `lessons/global-hotkeys-and-snapengine.md`.
See [[zero_roundtrip_pattern]].

**semantic_search RAG: CoreML MiniLM SHIPPED and works (2026-06-02).** `bin/vault-rag` chunks
notes into header-aware sections and embeds via **all-MiniLM-L6-v2 as a CoreML model on the
Neural Engine** (hand-rolled WordPiece tokenizer, input_ids+attention_mask [1,256] → hidden_states
[1,256,384], mean-pool + L2-normalize, cosine=dot). Verified: "AppleScriptObjC ASObjC" surfaces
`concepts/asobjc.md` at **#2** (was NOT in the top 30 with NLEmbedding), and `fm semantic_search`
returns a correct grounded answer quoting the file. Warm queries ~1.2 s; cold embed of the wiki
~64 s one-time. Build: `bin/build-minilm.sh` → python3.12 venv, **pin `transformers==4.44.2`
`torch==2.5.1` `numpy<2`** (numpy 2 breaks coremltools' int-cast → "only 0-dimensional arrays can
be converted to Python scalars"; coremltools dropped ONNX input so that route is dead — torch.jit.trace
+ numpy<2 is the path). `bin/minilm-convert.py` does the trace+convert. Model lives at
`models/minilm/MiniLM.mlpackage`+`vocab.txt` (gitignored); compiled `.mlmodelc` cached at
~/.cache/apple/. **Wart:** `git reset --hard` (the deploy step) bumps file mtimes → vault-rag's
mtime-keyed cache (v3) cold-re-embeds on the next query (~64 s one-time per deploy); fix later by
keying the cache on content hash instead of mtime. [[zero_roundtrip_pattern]]

**DEPLOY GOTCHA — ALWAYS `git fetch` before `reset --hard origin/main` on the Mini, and verify
the BUILT ARTIFACT, not just `BUILD EXIT=0` (burned ~an hour 2026-06-02).** `git reset --hard
origin/main` resets to the LAST-FETCHED remote-tracking ref. If you skip `git fetch`, that ref is
FROZEN, so `build.sh` recompiles STALE source every time — the build succeeds (`BUILD EXIT=0`) but
on old code, and the running app never changes. Symptom: pushed fix after pushed fix, none take
effect. Always: `git -C …/apple fetch -q origin main && git -C …/apple reset --hard origin/main`,
then confirm the change is actually in the compiled binary, e.g. `strings build/…/FoundationModelsChat
| grep "Edit System Prompt"` — `BUILD EXIT=0` alone proves nothing about WHICH source built.

**Speed (M2 Pro Mini):** model itself ~1 s for a sentence; Syncthing round-trip adds
~4–11 s. **Guardrails are aggressive** — expect refusals (hard `guardrailViolation` +
soft in-content declines); personal-info recall trips it. Deploy to the Mini with
`git reset --hard origin/main` (the deploy node diverges via its own auto-regen commits,
so `pull --ff-only` fails). Full doc: `wiki/concepts/on-device-ml.md`. See [[zero_roundtrip_pattern]].

# FM tools — giving the on-device LLM hands (FoundationModels tool-calling)

`bin/fm` / `fm-chat` today is a closed-book chatbot: it answers from the ~3B model's own
weights, nothing else. FoundationModels ships a **`Tool` protocol** — the model can call
Swift functions mid-generation and fold the results back into its answer. That turns the
chat from "what the model remembers" into "what the model can *go find out*" — grounded,
current, and specific to this fleet.

## How it fits our architecture (the elegant part)

Tools register on the `LanguageModelSession` **on the Mini, in-process**. So when the laptop
sends one prompt over Syncthing, the Mini's FM session can call local tools (read a file,
run an embedding search, read the climate JSON) *during that single generation* and return
the finished, grounded answer. **Tool calls do not bounce back to the laptop** — it's still
one Syncthing round-trip, no matter how many tools fire. The transport cost we measured
(~4–11s) doesn't multiply.

Implementation: extend `bin/fm.swift` to register a set of `Tool` conformers and pass them
to `LanguageModelSession(tools:instructions:)`. `fm-worker` stays unchanged (or gains a
`--tools` flag). Each tool's `call()` is a tiny Swift wrapper that either reads a file or
shells out to one of the `apple-*` CLIs already in `bin/`. Exact API surface gets verified at
build time on the Mini (FM is macOS-26-only; can't compile-test on the laptop).

## The security boundary (unchanged)

The worker's existing rule holds: **a job never carries a shell command, and FM never gets
an arbitrary-shell tool.** Tools are an *allowlist* of named, fixed-purpose Swift functions —
exactly like `panel-worker`'s registered-action allowlist. "Search this folder" is a tool;
"run this bash" is never a tool. Read-only tools first; any write/side-effect tool (send mail,
create reminder) gets added deliberately, one at a time.

## The catalog — grouped by what they reach

### A. On-device ML (already built as CLIs — these become tools almost for free)
| Tool | Wraps | "Chat can now…" |
|---|---|---|
| `semantic_search(query, folder)` | `apple-semantic-match` / `vault-grep` (NLEmbedding) | **RAG** — "find my notes about X" → grounds the answer in real files |
| `ocr(file)` | `vision-ocr` (Vision `VNRecognizeText`) | "what does this PDF/screenshot say?" |
| `image_similar(image, folder)` | `apple-image-similar` (Vision FeaturePrint) | "find the screenshot like this one / dupes" |
| `entities(text)` / `keywords(text)` | `apple-ner` / `apple-keywords` (NLTagger) | "who/what is named in this?" |
| `translate(text, lang)` | `apple-translate` (Translation framework) | "say that in Finnish" |
| `sentiment(text)` | `apple-sentiment` | tone/triage scoring |

All of these are on-device, no network, no cost — the same pedigree as FM itself.

### B. Fleet + system state (read a file or run a tiny query)
| Tool | Source | "Chat can now…" |
|---|---|---|
| `now()` | system clock | the model doesn't know the date/time — this fixes it (cheapest, highest-value first tool) |
| `home_climate()` | `~/work/comms/queue/homepod-climate/` JSON | "what's the temperature at home?" |
| `fleet_status()` | the `*-heartbeat.json` files | "is the Mini busy? is OCR running?" |
| `whisp_search(query)` | the whisp-transcripts corpus | "find where I talked about X on YouTube" |
| `mail_search(query)` | Mail SQLite (mail-flag pipeline infra) | "find emails from X" (read-only) |

### C. Apple system frameworks (Apple-native, read-only to start)
| Tool | Framework | "Chat can now…" |
|---|---|---|
| `calendar(range)` | EventKit | "what's on my calendar this week?" |
| `reminders()` | EventKit | "what's due?" |
| `contacts(name)` | Contacts | look up a person |

(These need TCC grants on the Mini; EventKit/Contacts prompts once, like the topbar grants.)

### Complement: structured output (`@Generable`)
Not a "tool" but the other half — annotate a Swift struct with `@Generable`/`@Guide` and FM
returns a **validated typed value** (constrained decoding, not parse-and-pray). This is what
makes FM a reliable *extractor* for the trigger→worker chassis: "pull the action items / the
invoice fields / the routing decision" → a struct, every time. Pairs naturally with tools
(a tool fetches text, structured output shapes the result).

## Recommended first batch (proves the three tool shapes)
1. **`now()`** — pure-compute tool, trivial, immediately useful (fixes "what day is it").
2. **`home_climate()`** — file-read tool against existing fleet data.
3. **`semantic_search(query, folder)`** — the flagship: on-device RAG via NLEmbedding, the
   one that makes the chat genuinely more than its weights.

If those three round-trip cleanly, the rest of the catalog is the same pattern repeated.

## Is FM the engine for the apple skill itself? (the real destination)

Yes — this is literally the apple skill's stated identity: *"the LLM-driven Automator."*
Until now the "LLM" driving it has been Claude (cloud). FM tool-calling means the apple
skill's own curated actions could be driven by an **on-device, Apple-native, zero-cost,
zero-network** model instead. You chat in plain language; FM picks the action and fills the
arguments; the action runs. That's the Automator brain, on-device. Three honest boundaries:

**1. Which tools — not all `bin/` scripts are equal.**
- ✅ **Read-only / compute / headless-batch** (OCR a folder, embed+search a vault, NER,
  translate, image-dedup, transcribe, mirror, summarize, classify) — perfect fit. These are
  what the apple skill calls "the LLM-driven Automator: any folder-batch transform." FM
  routes them beautifully.
- ⚠️ **Side-effecting UI automation** (Finder moves, app activation, window tiling, System
  Events keystrokes, sending Mail) — gated, one at a time, read-only-first. And the hard ban
  stands: **never give an LLM a System-Events-keystroke tool that fires on the machine
  someone is actively using** (see `feedback_never_ui_hijack_active_session`). Side effects go
  through side-channel pipelines (inbox files, the panel allowlist), not simulated keystrokes.

**2. Where it runs — FM is on the Mini, so it drives the *server-side* fleet.**
FM tools execute on the Mini, in-process. So FM-as-Automator-brain naturally drives the
**headless fleet** (OCR/embeddings/transcribe/mirror/translate) — not "activate an app on
the laptop I'm typing on," because that has to happen where the user is. The laptop can't
host its own FM node yet (macOS 15.6.1; FM needs 26). When the laptop is on 26, a local
fm-worker makes the same brain drive *local* actions too.

**3. It's an allowlist, not "run any script."**
FM never gets a "exec any bin/ tool" tool — that reintroduces the arbitrary-shell hole and
the UI-hijack risk. It gets a **curated set of named actions**, each a Swift `Tool` wrapper.
This is the *same allowlist* the **Apple Panel** (`apple-panel`) and **panel-worker** already
expose as cards-with-Run-buttons. So the clean unification is:

> **FM tool-calling = the natural-language front door to the Apple Panel action registry.**
> The Panel gives each capability a card + a Run button; FM lets you say it in words, picks
> the card, and fills the arg. Same curated, safe action set — two front doors.

**The capability ceiling (be honest):** a 3B model is a good *router over a defined action
set* and a good *summarize/classify/extract* engine — not a heavy multi-step reasoner. So the
realistic design is **tiered**: FM handles the fast/free/private/on-device common cases ("OCR
these, translate that, search my vault, which card fits this request"); Claude/cloud stays the
heavy reasoner for novel multi-step orchestration. FM doesn't replace Claude here — it makes
the *frequent, well-defined* automations free and local.

## See also
- [on-device-ml.md](on-device-ml.md) — the framework family + the fm-worker fleet plumbing
- [machine-card-protocol.md](machine-card-protocol.md) — where `fleet_status()` reads from
- [apple-panel](../../commands/apple-panel.md) / `bin/panel-worker` — the same curated action
  allowlist FM would route over in natural language
